locations.name: Artisans' Quarter
locations.playerDescription: The Artisans' Quarter is the industrial heart of Ubersreik. It lies to the east of the Grey Lady Road, on the north bank of the Teufel, where raw materials and finished goods are loaded and unloaded on wharves. By day the ringing sounds of hammers striking metal blends with the acrid stench of the town's tanners and chandlers. The quarter contains several slum districts at the periphery supporting taverns and cheap shops servicing the town's workers. Even at night the streets are rarely empty as workers relax after a hard day's graft.
locations.gmNotes: Since the Jungfreuds were ousted and their trade embargo began, coal has become scarce. Now the streets are full of apprentices on the scrounge for anything to burn.

locations.name: Bridge House Inn
locations.playerDescription:
Bridge House is perfectly situated in the centre of Ubersreik on the main thoroughfares near Ubersreik Bridge, offering spectacular views of the Dwarf-made marvel. The inn has large stables and a sizeable coach house, and also serves as Ubersreik's bustling post office. 

The inn has a spacious kitchen, a sizeable larder, two offices, two private dining rooms, and staff quarters. The two upper floors are set aside for private rooms, with rooms above the coach house and stables for visiting coachmen. The largest private room on the top floor commands an impressive view of Ubersreik Bridge. The lower floor has a broad taproom with several curtained booths for more clandestine meetings.
locations.gmNotes:
The inn is managed by Gunther Abend, a retired coachman, his wife Hanna, and their three children, plus nine other staff. An Altdorfer by birth, Abend has been very welcoming towards the visiting Imperial troops, upsetting his few local customers.
 Although locals rarely eat or drink here, balking at the prices, the fare is good, the portions generous, and the selection of beverages broad. Because of this, it is a common haunt for wealthier merchants, travellers, and those with coin to burn.
hooks: Gustav Schtupp, Gunther's postmaster, is a spy. He quietly intercepts mail passing through his hands, trafficking the juicier gossip in coded messages. Whether he serves now the Imperial Herald, House Bruner, or a darker master, is uncertain.

Gunther proudly maintains his independence, servicing coaches from three local Coaching Houses — Cannon Ball Express, Four Seasons, and Imperial Expressways. Elicha Hochs, a representative of the Four Seasons, is seeking capable folk to disrupt rival coaches and put pressure on Gunther to sell the inn to the Four Seasons for their exclusive use.

locations.name: Carpenters' Guild
locations.playerDescription: The Carpenters' Guild building's facade is cunningly wrought with complex wooden leaf scrollwork, framed by two pillars constructed from the trunks of great oak trees. The building houses guildmembers' demonstrations of their skill arrayed in the Masters' Hall, a long wood-panelled gallery used for ceremonial events and business meetings. Guildmembers' workshops are mostly located nearby.
locations.gmNotes: Ernst Zimmerman, the current guildmaster, is remarkably tall with a booming voice. He is missing a finger on his right hand from a mishap with a chisel as an apprentice. His speciality is cabinet making. He is a friend of the Burgomeister, a popular figure amongst the town's middle-classes, and a lay-member of the Cult of Sigmar.
hooks: Zimmerman is leading a double life, moonlighting as a thief. Much of the guild's seeming affluence is a result of his illicit indiscretions. As a cabinet maker, he has access to his clients' homes and uses this to scout future burglaries. Some of his customers are growing suspicious, so he is on the lookout for bodyguards, or possibly scapegoats...

Quality timber is hard to secure given the demand for wood to burn now that coal is scarce in Ubersreik. The party are hired by Zimmerman to accompany him into the woods in search of a particular grove, little realising it is home to a small herd of Beastmen driven into the area by something bigger...

locations.name: Cordelia's Apothecary
locations.playerDescription: Cordelia's Apothecary lies on a small, cobbled platz at the end of the Wizard's Way. A painted wooden mortar and pestle hang above a stout wooden door. Garlands of sweet-smelling flowers and herbs are strung above the wooden door in the hope of enticing more customers.
locations.gmNotes:
Cordelia Wesselingh is a handsome woman with silver hair who has maintained the shop for decades. She is a kind, friendly soul, always ready to lend an ear, making her a good source of gossip (though nothing salacious). Her prices are fair, and she offers discounts to customers of good standing. 
Unknown to most, Cordelia apprenticed in the Jade College in Altdorf, though she lacked the strength to become a full wizard. She remains well-disposed towards the Colleges.
hooks: Cordelia is friendly with the local network of Hedgefolk. Ida Vernt, a recently arrived Hedgewitch, is concerned over malicious spirits in the area that are beyond her capabilities. Aiding Ida would earn Cordelia's trust.

Cordelia hides a deeper secret; she provides intelligence to the Grey Order of wizards. Her shop's cellar hides a secret entrance to Christoph Engel's tower. When she finds the door open with a bloody trail leading into the passageway, she knows the wizard must need help and looks for someone brave and discreet enough to investigate.

locations.name: Locksmith's Guild
locations.playerDescription: A narrow building with steel-barred windows, this guildhouse is maintained by Ubersreik's only locksmith, Ludwig Schlüsselfert. The locksmith only works for a few hours a day, and only four days a week, making it a challenge to find him. The ground floor is his workshop, with tools neatly hanging around the walls. Upstairs are his personal quarters, a small parlour and surprisingly sumptuous bedchambers.
locations.gmNotes: Ludwig Schlüsselfert is a cantankerous old curmudgeon in his eighth decade. Fiercely litigious, he has exercised his right to refuse membership to any visiting locksmiths, ensuring he has an absolute monopoly (except for Dwarf craftsmen). He regularly hires a team to check the locks of buildings in Ubersreik for non-sanctioned work. Should he discover any illegal locks, he will summon the Watch to remove them (and charge extra to replace them). His lawyer, Melina Spirren-Hirsch, is on retainer.
hooks: Schlüsselfert is, in truth, a member and blessed priest of the Crooked Fingers sect of the Cult of Ranald. Though he has no apprentice locksmiths, he uses his cellar to train aspiring thieves in the fine art of lockpicking, should they be good Ranaldans and able to pay.

After several houses are broken into, Schlüsselfert hires the party to check a number locks for his customers. Though he had nothing to do with it, he cannot afford to have the Watch asking questions, so the players need to solve the crime or secure a scapegoat, and quickly.

locations.name: Metalworkers' Guild
locations.playerDescription: The Metalworkers' Guildhouse is a squat, unassuming, soot-stained building just off the Bögenhafen road. It is surrounded by forges, smithies, and workshops that ring with the sound of hammers on steel from dawn to dusk. The interior of the guildhouse is dark, and low-ceilinged, an attempt to appeal to the city's Dwarf populace.
locations.gmNotes: The Dwarf craftsmen are polite to a fault, but do not view their inferior 'shortbeard' counterparts as rivals. Petronilla Merkle is the current master, a short woman with broad shoulders and calloused palms. Though generally stoic, when roused to anger her temper is fearsome. As she is often busy in her workshop, the guildhouse is generally staffed by one of her skittish apprentices.
hooks: Johann Messing, one of Merkle's rivals in the guild, is seeking to mount a coup. He is looking for adventurers to engage in a little river piracy. If the party can hijack one of the Jungfreud's (well guarded) coal barges before it enters the Hagercryb Canal, and bring it safely to Ubersreik, they will be richly rewarded.

Following a terrible accident in one of the city's forges, Merkle is looking for someone to quietly investigate the explosion. Given the rumours of flickering green flames and unholy screams, volunteers are thin on the ground. Should the players investigate, they will be noticed by Watch Sergeant Knopf, who is subtly ignoring the explosion, and by the Skaven who are paying him to do so.

locations.name: Satrioli's Sausage Shop
locations.playerDescription: Satrioli's Sausage Shop is a thriving business that offers a wide selection of sausages, cured meats, imported cheeses, and other delicacies. It occupies the ground floor of a stone building. There are a number of tables and benches outside the shop, but many customers take their food away to eat at home or in their place of work. Gino Satrioli, a charming Tilean, tends the shop with his wife Carla and their son Furio. They employ a gaggle of Halflings to assist with day-to-day tasks.
locations.gmNotes: The wooden storey above is rented out by the large family of Halflings. Beneath the shop, there is a sizeable cellar used as a storeroom which also has a shrine to Myrmidia. Rumours suggest many of the sausages are in fact made by the Halflings, not by the Satriolis, but given the diminutive folk's reputation for culinary skill, nobody is complaining. In truth, Satrioli's is a front for the infamous Lowhaven clan of Halflings. Under the leadership of Mercy Lowhaven, they are muscling in on the other organised crime in town and are always on the lookout for more help.
hooks: The Lowhaven clan's standard operating procedure is to get someone in debt, before exploiting that weakness, so if any members of the party are looking for a loan...

'White Gold' is the most profitable product in Satrioli's, a particularly creamy cheese imported from Tilea. Recently, their supplier has signed an exclusive contract with Harzert's, a rival cheesemonger. Mercy Lowhaven is willing to pay handsomely for Harzert's supply, and won't ask any questions. Securing the contract for Satrioli's would earn a favour from the Lowhavens.

locations.name: Wandiene Rookery
locations.playerDescription: Of all Ubersreik's slums, Wandiene rookery is the largest and most notorious. It lies in the north-west of the Artisans' Quarter, packed tight to the high town-walls. Its tall, unstable houses lean precariously against each other, and any available space between is filled with shacks and makeshift hovels. The few paths and alleyways are narrow, gloomy, filthy, and untrod by the Watch.
locations.gmNotes: The rookery is uncensused and massively overcrowded, and is known for its many bawds, thieves, and ne'erdowells. Its houses have no access to Ubersreik's extensive sewers. Guido Falck, a retired and decorated captain loyal to Duke Sigismund Jungfreud, has retreated here. He leads a resistance of over 50 fighters against the 'Altdorf invasion' from the depths of the slums. He is a patient man, and will not attack his enemy openly.
hooks: Falck plans to blow up Black Rock Castle during an important gathering of Altdorf luminaries. He has access to the sewers beneath the castle and needs unfortunate fools to buy large quantities of blackpowder then deliver it to him. Of course, when the Watch investigate, Falck expects it's the blackpowder buyers that will be pursued, giving him time to retreat.

Karolus Dichens, author and journalist, is researching his next book, 'Nonnie Verdreh'. He wants a tour of Wandiene, but can't find anyone he trusts to guide him. He hovers near its periphery taking notes, then retires to the Bridge House Inn. He doesn't have much money, but will offer to include the party in his next book as incidental characters if they protect him.

locations.name: The Worshipful Guild of Cutlers
locations.playerDescription: This guild has grown significantly in wealth and influence. In addition to forks and knives, they have begun selling weaponry. The building comprises the old guildhouse, which has been expanded to include a large forge and workshop area, and a small showroom. Here shoppers can purchase blades, which are of high quality and surprisingly good value.
locations.gmNotes: While the bylaws of Ubersreik specify that only members of the Metalworkers' Guild may make swords, the cutlers have exploited a loophole regarding how the handle is attached to the tang, allowing them to class their blades as knives (albeit knives with blades several feet long). The guildmaster is Rudy Schlau, a skilled politician. Unknown to almost all, Dordean Mournflair is the secret behind his guild's success. Dordean is an Elf who has called Ubersreik home for centuries. Dordean was spurned by the Metalworkers' Guild due to their Dwarf sympathies, so the Cutlers (who now worship Vaul) are benefitting from his calling.
hooks: Petronilla Merkle, guildmaster of the Metalworkers' Guild, is livid at the Cutlers' circumvention of the town's bylaws, especially as they are producing a superior product for a lower cost. She is very interested in finding out the secrets of their methods and, if possible, destroying their guildhouse. Any morally flexible parties could profit by assisting her.

Recently, Dordean's sibling arrived in Ubersreik, eager to persuade Dordean to return to Ulthuan. The party are offered a generous payment to out Dordean as an Elf, capitalising on resentment of Elf interference.

locations.name: Black Rock
locations.playerDescription: Black Rock is less a district, and more a castle complex named for the dark granite that forms its ancient walls. It dominates Ubersreik, covering almost an eighth of the town. It is ringed by huge parapets connecting directly to the town's walls, making it integral to Ubersreik's defence. The invading troops from Altdorf made Black Rock their home, tearing down the silver and blue banners of the von Jungfreuds and replacing them with Altdorf's red and blue, a gesture of disrespect many locals find galling.
locations.gmNotes: For centuries it was the bastion of the Jungfreuds. A secure tunnel leads from Black Rock to the Magnus Tower, allowing for troops and messages to pass. Within Black Rock's walls lies a bustling community, a town within a town. It contains grain stores, workshops, museums, chapels, housing, animal pens, and more. When Ubersreik was seized, any remaining local staff were forcibly ejected, leading to much resentment. All five Altdorf regiments are barracked here, though rarely more than a thousand soldiers are present at any one time.
hooks: A small group of locals is determined to wreak vengeance on the Altdorf forces for evicting them from their homes, and driving out the rightful rulers of Ubersreik. They are looking for accomplices to sneak into the castle and poison the garrison's supplies, and General von Dabernick's dinner, with Spritzenberries, a naturally powerful laxative.

locations.name: Black Rock Castle
locations.playerDescription: Black Rock Castle is enormous, easily the largest fortification in the southern Vorbergland. It is a warren of halls, salons, barracks, and private chambers. The castle's corridors, which once thronged with servants, now ring with the hollow echo of the invaders' footsteps. The huge fireplace in the Great Hall — once a beacon welcoming guests — lies empty and unlit.
locations.gmNotes: Beneath the castle lie the extensive Ubersreik dungeons, where many Jungfreud enemies spent their remaining years. General Jendrick von Dabernick now rules the castle, and he puts on a good show of ruling the rest of Ubersreik with all the power and none of the responsibility of a duke. Von Dabernick is the scion of a minor noble line with a historic grudge against the Jungfreuds. An abrasive presence, he is determined to root out any sympathisers for the exiled Jungfreuds, which earns him few friends locally.

locations.name: Grauer Palast
locations.playerDescription: The Grauer Palast is a squat keep to the north-east of Black Rock Castle. It contains the largest ballroom in the Vorbergland, and is where the Jungfreuds once conducted their social functions and weddings.
locations.gmNotes: The keep was long used as the official residence of the Baron of Lady's Vale, the heir to the duchy of Ubersreik. It now houses Lady Emmanuelle Nacht, the Imperial Herald, and the true power in Ubersreik. The daughter of Duke Gregor Nacht, an ex-ambassador to Grand Cathay, her life changed when her father was assassinated six years ago. She is investigating the 'Purple Hand', a mysterious group she believes is responsible for her father's death, and is in Ubersreik at Emperor Karl-Franz's personal request to oversee the pacification of the town.

locations.name: Saint Arnold's Chapel
locations.playerDescription: Black Rock's chapel to Sigmar is dedicated to Saint Arnold. As with most Sigmarite temples, its walls form the plan of a hammer, although the ravages of time and subsidence have left the nave somewhat crooked. Its walls remain stout, though slightly crumbling. It contains a beautiful stained-glass window from Nuln, and many fine carvings depicting Sigmar's victories. Since the occupying forces took Black Rock, few now attend Sister Habercorn's services.
locations.gmNotes: Sister Habercorn, previously the personal confessor to the Jungfreuds, maintains her chapel and performs her sermons to the near-empty chapel. Unbeknownst to the occupiers, a network of tunnels lie beneath the chapel, lined with Orc graffiti from a past invasion. Sister Habercorn and the von Jungfreuds are the only ones aware of the tunnels' existence. When the Altdorf forces arrived, Graf Sigismund von Jungfreud fled, but his youngest son, Wendelin, was overlooked. Sister Habercorn found him and hid him in the tunnels beneath the chapel. She now keeps him fed and watered, and is desperate to smuggle the boy from the castle.
hooks: In desperation, Sister Habercorn has turned to the party to help her smuggle young Lord Wendelin out of Black Rock. If he is caught, the Altdorfers may injure or even kill him, given their general's attitude to the von Jungfreuds. They could seek out the rumoured secret passageway, or try to brazenly smuggle him out a main gate.

locations.name: Lokhid's Ammunition Depot
locations.playerDescription: Lokhid's Ammunition Depot is a stout stone building with thick walls and a reinforced door. It lies within Black Rock's walls, close to the main gate. The depot stores gunpowder, shot, and other munitions for the Altdorf garrison. It is heavily guarded, with soldiers posted both inside and outside the building at all times.
locations.gmNotes: The depot is managed by Master Gunner Fritz Lokhid, a grizzled veteran of many campaigns. He is a stickler for safety, and enforces strict rules regarding the handling and storage of munitions. The depot has a number of secret compartments and hidden rooms, known only to Lokhid and his most trusted assistants.
hooks: Lokhid is secretly sympathetic to the von Jungfreuds, and is looking for a way to sabotage the Altdorf garrison. He is willing to pay handsomely for anyone who can help him steal a significant quantity of gunpowder from the depot without being caught.

A group of Skaven agents has infiltrated Black Rock, seeking to steal munitions for their own nefarious purposes. The party could be hired by Lokhid to root out these infiltrators, or they could be approached by the Skaven themselves to assist in their theft.

locations.name: Dawihafen
locations.playerDescription: Dawihafen, Ubersreik's Dwarf Quarter, is a tightly knit community of local Dwarfs. Only a handful of Humans and Halflings inhabit the area; mostly just the town's 1000 or so Dwarfs gather here. The Dwarf population largely keep to themselves.
locations.gmNotes: Ubersreik has maintained close ties with the Dwarfs since Magnus the Pious appealed to them for their aid in rebuilding the town following the Great War Against Chaos. In addition to the soaring bridge, the town's walls and many of its stone buildings are of solid Dwarf construction.

locations.name: Borgun's Brewery
locations.playerDescription: Butted up against the Axe and Hammer lies Borgun's Brewery, Ubersreik's only Dwarf brewer and purveyor of strong, dark ales. The brewery consists of a number of discrete stone buildings, each housing a distinct stage of the brewing process. There is a mill, a mash-house, a boiler room, and a number of storage sheds. A covered passageway leads directly to The Axe and Hammer, Borgun's biggest customer.
locations.gmNotes: Pink-faced Brewmaster Borgun Foambeard, who proudly claims to be a cousin to master brewer Josef Bugman, makes a number of ales, including Crownpeak, Old Subterranean, and Skullsplitter. Foambeard is assisted by his two brothers, Hargan and Dwargun, and his grey-bearded uncle, Glavic Boarhand. Glavic spends most of his time drinking and reminiscing about when his grandfather ran the brewery, wounding Foambeard with every careless word.
hooks: The party discover that Foambeard is not, in truth, related to Josef Bugman, but has made the claim falsely to boost sales. Should he be confronted publicly, he would be shamed and would likely take the Slayer Oath. Perhaps the Characters can leverage this knowledge in some way that would be profitable?

Sahra Tanner, a human brewer from the Artisan Quarter, is jealous of Foambeard's success. She has poisoned a number of his barrels, bound for a reception on the Hill, with warpstone, little realising the danger this poses. Can the party intercept the contaminated beer before the nobles begin to drink from it?

locations.name: Harataken Hold
locations.playerDescription: This suite of rooms within a large, squat block is the home of the Harataki clan of Dwarfs. A once noble line, they have over the years sold off rooms and sections of the building to fund ill-fated expeditions to reclaim their ancestral Hold, leaving them with only a handful of rooms to their name.
locations.gmNotes: Queen Vilda is the clan leader and has overseen the dwindling resources of her clan for over a century. Though her family have become increasingly desperate, she is determined to regain both their Lost Hold, Karak Branar, and their lost status amongst other Dwarfs. As such, she is alert to any insult or disrespect, and keeps her clan's Book of Grudges close to hand.
hooks: Queen Vilda is planning another expedition to Karak Branar's ruins, which lie to the north of Grey Lady Pass. She needs a small party to range ahead, scouting and assessing the strength of the Greenskin forces arrayed against them. She will reward any volunteers handsomely, if she successfully retakes the Hold.

Gjur Farlson, Karak Azgaraz's ambassador, publicly supports the Harataki clan's aspirations, but lacks the resources to offer any tangible support. If the players have any means to convince the ambassador to offer funds or troops, they will earn Queen Vilda's respect (though they may earn Karak Azgaraz's ire in the process).

locations.name: Khazalgirt
locations.playerDescription: Beneath Dawihafen, a network of sturdy Dwarf-built tunnels forms its own subterranean street network. The tunnels are regular, well-constructed, and well-lit, not to mention well-patrolled. A large shrine to Grimnir lies at the nexus of the passages — a natural meeting point for local Slayers to gather.
locations.gmNotes: The tunnels lead to most major Dwarf locations in Ubersreik. They are separate and discrete from both the Human sewers, and the Dwarfs' own sewer system, which lies deeper underground. Should any non-Dwarfs find their way into the network, they will be politely, if forcibly, ejected. Repeat offenders will not be treated gently.
hooks: When the party stumble across the body of a rat-like beastman, they discover a neatly detailed map of the Khazalgirt, with a crudely drawn addition indicating another tunnel network seemingly connecting to the Dwarfs' passages. The party could warn the Dwarfs, or they could keep the map and perhaps use it to rob a number of wealthy Dwarf merchants.

When the players wipe out a small party of Goblins beyond the town walls, they discover the entrance to a tunnel leading beneath the Khazalgirt. Should they follow the tunnel they will see it leads to a number of barrels, full of blackpowder with the letters 'B-O-M' crudely daubed on the side, and the fuses are already lit!

locations.name: Lord Gazul's Underearth
locations.playerDescription: Deep beneath the Khazalgirt, at the end of a long tunnel, lies Lord Gazul's Underearth. Entry is through a guarded fifty-foot high cave mouth carved with a yawning Dwarf face. Within is an enormous, earth-floored cavern with thousands of carved stone sarcophagi, each grouped by clan. In the centre of the cavern stands a twenty-foot statue of Gazul, great guardian of the dead. Gazul looks troubled, and leans heavily on a great runesword.
locations.gmNotes: Nargrimi the Quiet ensures Gazul's teachings are remembered. The ancient Dwarf is Karugromthi, a living ancestor. She tends to the Dwarf dead in Ubersreik, and consoles the bereaved. There are none alive in Ubersreik who can remember when Nargrimi last left the cavern.
hooks: Reman Wardas and Gantz Ganev learn of the motherlode of corpses from a drunk Harataki Dwarf. They steal a map and dig a tunnel to the Underearth. Realising the place is well guarded, they seek a party of capable folk to create a diversion. However, on the day of the planned robbery, the nearby river floods, flushing everyone into the Underearth, leaving them with a lot of explaining to do.

Nargrimi is not just a living ancestor, she is the true Queen of Karak Zanda, a Lost Hold. When news arrives that her former home was uncovered, she wishes to speak to outsiders. She explains that her Lost Hold must never be investigated, and that no Dwarf with honour may ever approach Karak Zanda. She will provide 10 GC to any party who closes all routes to the ruins.

locations.name: Nordwander and Son's Expeditionary Supplies
locations.playerDescription: A large, low-ceilinged building, Nordwander and Son's prides itself on selling everything its clientele will need to mount expeditions into the Grey Mountains. A one-stop-shop for mountaineering and camping, it carries pitons, ropes, mallets, rations, tents, and anything else a party may need. Despite their broader clientele, the shop is still set up with Dwarfs in mind, with low ceilings and broad aisles.
locations.gmNotes: The shop initially catered exclusively to Dwarfs, but word of the quality of their gear spread. They now stock clothing and tools for non-Dwarfs. Gudrum Nordwander is good natured for a Dwarf and happy to share his high-quality wares, though he is quick to lecture customers expressing ignorance on mining or climbing. Belorn, his energetic son, assists in the shop and dreams of leaving Ubersreik. He will gab excitedly to all customers, quizzing them on where they are going and their plans.
hooks: Belorn Nordwander offers the party a discount if he can accompany them on their expedition. Though charming and intelligent, Belorn has little experience of life beyond Ubersreik's walls, and will be something of a hindrance, a fact to which he is entirely oblivious.

Legendary explorer Ernst von Schäkeldorf is planning an expedition to climb Mount Frugelhorn, and the party are to travel with him. He has managed to upset Nordwander by expecting a hefty discount based on his fame. Can the party resolve the tensions and bring everyone to a mutually satisfactory agreement, or will the expedition be called off?

locations.name: Vorgim's Herbs and Liquors
locations.playerDescription: Vorgim's Herbs and Liquors is a small, cluttered shop filled with the scent of dried herbs and strong spirits. The shelves are lined with jars of various herbs, roots, and tinctures, as well as bottles of potent liquors and medicinal concoctions. The shop is dimly lit, with a single window letting in a slant of light.
locations.gmNotes: Vorgim Stonebeard is a knowledgeable Dwarf herbalist and apothecary. He is well-versed in the medicinal properties of various plants and herbs, and is happy to share his knowledge with customers. Vorgim is also a skilled distiller, producing a range of potent liquors that are popular among both Dwarfs and Humans alike.
hooks: Vorgim is seeking rare herbs that grow only in the Grey Mountains. He offers a generous reward to anyone who can bring him samples of these plants, which he believes have powerful medicinal properties.

A rival herbalist has been spreading rumours about Vorgim's products, claiming they are ineffective and overpriced. Vorgim is looking for someone to investigate and put a stop to these rumours, restoring his reputation.

locations.name: Teubrücke (The Docks)
locations.playerDescription: Ubersreik docks spread the length of the Teufel in the centre of the town. The Docks comprise the usual mixture of wharves, warehouses, inns, guildhouses, cheap services, and tax and customs offices. Slums lie behind the bustle of these buildings — the housing quality dipping with every step taken from the river.
locations.gmNotes: Though officially listed as Teubrücke in the town's charter, this quarter, and all its attached slum and warehouse districts, is generally referred to as 'The Docks'.

locations.name: Boatmen's Guild
locations.playerDescription: The Boatmen's Guild meets in a converted two-storey riverfront warehouse on the southside of the Teufel. The lower floor has a subsidised tavern and dormitory for its members with almost everything sold at cost, and several private rooms also available. The food and drink is decent and plentiful. The upper floor, looking down over the drinking hall, contains the guild's offices and the guildmaster's quarters.
locations.gmNotes: The guild is affiliated with the Boatmen's Guilds of Auerswald, Kemperbad, and Altdorf, giving members benefits across the guilds. Guildmaster Karsten Rugger is a cantankerous old man, though still respected. Rumours that he runs the majority of the river smuggling in Upper Teufel have never been proven. Robbo Brambledown, a Halfling, runs the kitchens.
hooks: The guild's working relationship with Altdorf has kept them neutral in the town's political turmoil. For their part, the Altdorf troops have been turning a blind eye to any smuggling they discover. Should this be known publicly, it would undermine the authority of the Altdorfers, but will anger the guild.

A shipment of brandy from Bretonnia is due to be smuggled into Ubersreik tonight. Nixie Dunkelstange is overseeing things, but cannot use guild members, as she suspects someone is feeding information to Geldfinger in Customs House. It's a dangerous venture, but profit awaits those willing to take the risk.

locations.name: The Crooked Hammer
locations.playerDescription: The Crooked Hammer is a slightly seedy, rough-looking tavern typical of those found in the Teubrücke. It serves a variety of hard spirits and watery ales, at cheap prices. It is an open secret that the drinking house is a front for a gambling den. To the rear of the building, they operate a soup kitchen, providing basic sustenance to the poor and needy of Ubersreik.
locations.gmNotes: The gambling den is run by the Crosses, adherents of Ranald, the God of Trickery, who view such activities as holy work. Gert Hunder runs the bar and acts as a lookout. Silvi Kreutzhame, a formidable woman in her 50s, is the leader of the Ranaldan cult in Ubersreik. The authorities tolerate the gambling, in part because of the charitable work and because many influential citizens frequent the Hammer.
hooks: While most are aware of the gambling den, less well known is the clandestine fencing operation run behind the book-keeper's office. Here, the Crooked Fingers buy, sell, and trade stolen goods. If the party has been robbed, their goods will likely be there, if they can talk their way past the Ranaldans.

Dannel Meer, legendary thief, is putting together a crew to raid Black Rock Castle. He claims taxes from the Duchy of Ubersreik are simply piling up unclaimed in the vaults. There is a fortune there for the taking. Assuming Meer is correct...

locations.name: Customs House
locations.playerDescription: All tax collected in Ubersreik comes through Customs House, a large, sturdy building with a commanding view over the wharves and the river-traffic. All boats unloading in the town pay a tax of one silver coin plus an additional charge depending upon the cargo, as well as potential docking fees. Wagons of trading goods pay their taxes at the town gates.
locations.gmNotes:
Ernst Geldfinger runs the operation. He is a thuggish man in his 40s who tightly controls his clerks. He has a reputation for meticulous detail and unimpeachable honesty.

TAXING SITUATION: Before the Jungfreuds were removed, taxes were collated here and transferred to Black Rock. The right to gather these taxes lies solely with the duke of Ubersreik, but there is no duke. No one knows who should collect them. General von Dabernick favours enforcing tax collection, legal or not, while Lady Nacht prefers to organise a legal and stable replacement for the duke.
hooks: When the party witness Detlef Schädler, one of Geldfinger's clerks, murdered en route to his post, they see an opportunity. If they hide the body, they could take his place and pocket the day's taxes. All they need to do is fool the town guards and the merchants, keep the body hidden, and avoid whomever killed Schädler.

Geldfinger has noted a drop off on tax revenue on brandy, due to a smuggling ring. He suspects one of his clerks is on the payroll, so he is looking to hire 'independent contractors' to investigate quietly and shut down the operation. He is willing to pay handsomely.

locations.name: Dockers' Arm
locations.playerDescription: This sprawling, timber and lathe tavern caters almost exclusively to the town's stevedores and teamsters, who have a monopoly on the loading and unloading of all trade goods in Ubersreik. Without paying their fees, none of your cargo moves. At any one time, several teams of Dockers will be drinking in the tavern, and many more will be working the wharves.
locations.gmNotes: The Dockers' Arms is effectively the Guildhouse for the Dockers' Guild. It is owned and managed by the guildmaster: Wilhelm 'Big Willi' Docker, a giant of a man with arms bigger than most men's thighs. The lower floor is given over to two tap rooms and a small kitchen. Upstairs is the Docker family living quarters.
hooks: Aloysius Thorncobble III, a Halfling merchant has employed the party. He is in dispute with the Dockers' Guild, who are refusing to unload for him until he settles an outstanding debt. As he believes he paid the debt (to the Dockers' Guild in Altdorf), he is unwilling to do so. As the party begin to unload his barge, a group of dockers arrive to point out the error in their ways.

Little Willi, Big Willi's even-taller son, has been smuggling luxury foodstuffs for the Lowhaven Clan. But when the Watch confiscated his last load on Geldfinger's orders, that left him owing the Halflings a lot of money. He is willing to offer free Guild Membership to the party if they help him break into the warehouse and steal the goods back.

locations.name: Grail Chapel
locations.playerDescription: The exterior of the Bretonnian Grail Chapel is unassuming, a modest warehouse. Only the innocuous wooden inscriptions of fleur-de-lys along the eaves mark it as anything special. Within the walls, however, the building is sumptuous. Its walls and columns are intricately carved and beautifully painted, redolent with frescoes depicting legends of the Lady of the Lake, and brave knights of Bretonnian Lore.
locations.gmNotes: The building was used as an internment camp decades ago during the Fifth Parravon War. The Bretonnian captives decorated the chapel, which has been maintained by the Carpenters' Guild ever since. Hugo is the only permanent resident, an ancient Bretonnian with a white beard and kind eyes, whom local children are convinced was once a knight.
hooks: Hugo was, in fact, a knight, but he left Bretonnia in disgrace. A recent visitor, Sir Pierre De L'Arbaque, recognised the old man and has forcibly ejected him from his home. Hugo is determined to fight the much younger Pierre to reclaim his honour, but the party are convinced that if he does, he will be slaughtered.

Nils Scherzer, an agitator, has been whipping up a frenzy of anti-Bretonnian sentiment. He has raised a mob, intent on driving Bretonnians out of Ubersreik. He plans to burn the chapel to the ground, killing those within. There is no time to summon the Watch, only the party can intervene!

locations.name: The Guild of Boatbuilders and Chandlers
locations.playerDescription: This unassuming wooden building not far from Ubersreik's two dry docks on the southside of the river houses the offices for the combined Guild of Boatbuilders and Chandlers. Although called the Guild of Boatbuilders and Chandlers, the guild doesn't actually build boats or ships. It builds barges, which have flat bottoms for shallow-river travel.
locations.gmNotes: Thirty years ago, the two small guilds combined forces to amplify their voices. Today, the guild is still small, but undeniably powerful. Kurt Prochnow is the current Guildmaster, a lean, muscled man in his early 30s. He is driven and intelligent with a voracious appetite for new approaches to construction, currently experimenting with metal and stone. His thriving business landed him the unwanted title of 'Most Eligible Bachelor of Ubersreik'.
hooks: Prochnow's latest prototype was stolen by river pirates. Should the riverwardens take it down, they will likely damage the boat or ask awkward questions, so he is willing to pay handsomely for a party to quietly recover the vessel, with a significant bonus should it be unscathed.

Prochnow's travels and letters are a facade. He is a member of a widespread Cult, the Fractured Eye, who pursue knowledge at all costs. Beneath the guildhouse he keeps a profane and illegal library. He seeks a particular scroll from the Temple of Verena, and would very much like some patsies to steal it for him.

locations.name: The Hog Pit
locations.playerDescription: The Schwarzehalle slum's Hog Pit is a sprawling series of open pig pens. The pigs dine on the town's scraps and filth, which are sold to swineherds by enterprising gong farmers. Citizens wishing to cross the Hog Pit use a series of elevated wooden platforms. These boards are treacherous, and more than one burgher has slipped, falling into the mud, waste, and pigs below.
locations.gmNotes: Gart Fünke, an old farmer, is the Hog Pit's most influential man. Theoretically, any citizen can keep pigs in the Pit, but in practice they need Fünke's approval, which he only gives with the promise of purchasing any pig 'feed' directly from him. Fünke ensures his racket is unchallenged by providing the local Watch with a ready supply of pork.
hooks: Dirk Schwengen, a protagonist who charges a toll to cross the Hog Pit, offers a choice: pay him, or end up in the muck.

Rumours claim Fünke feeds his pigs mortal remains. Fünke recently provided 'pork' to Satrioli's Sausage Shop, leading to whispers that he disposes bodies for the Lowhavens. When the Ghost of Benno Nusbaum haunts his daughter, she seeks help to retrieve his remains from the Hog Pit without alienating the Halfling criminals who put it there.

locations.name: The Kat House
locations.playerDescription: A stylised brass cat hangs above the Kat House, a dockside brothel dedicated to Katya, the Goddess of Disarming Beauty. The sizeable four-storey building caters to clientèle of all species and classes, and is protected by ever-present bouncers. Although most of its staff present as female, all tastes are catered for.
locations.gmNotes: Frau Jalla Krump, a solidly built woman in her 50s, handles all the day-to-day business. Krump is entirely beholden to Adelheidis 'Alisha' Keller, a young, blessed priestess of Katya who is committed to converting followers sworn to a single god to a polytheistic path. Alisha has formed close relations with the new watch captain, Andrea Pfeffer, and provides intelligence on those she believes are cultists of the Dark Gods, but only if she believes their souls are irrevocably lost.
hooks: The Kat House is ablaze. Onlookers panic, and a number of Alisha's staff, as well as some wealthy patrons, are trapped in the burning building. It's a deathtrap, but helping could be profitable, and possibly troublesome when evidence seems to point to an outraged Initiate of the Cult of Sigmar.

Albrecht Horsten, a wealthy grain merchant, is a frequent visitor. Alisha believes he has fallen to the Prince of Pleasure, so he, noting her suspicion, has placed a bounty on her head. Alisha needs an escort to the Precinct to meet with Captain Pfeffer, but a high bounty can be very tempting...

locations.name: Rugger's Boarding House
locations.playerDescription: Rugger's is Ubersreik's cheapest inn, and for good reason: the beds are infested and the common room mouldy and damp. The lower floor has a dirty kitchen, a creaky dining hall, and the common room. The upper floor squeezes four private rooms (each with two double bunks) and the proprietor's room into a tiny space.
locations.gmNotes: Anna Rugger, known on the docks as Gram'ma, is the aging proprietor of the boarding house. She is married to the master of the Boatmen's Guild, Karsten. Because of this, anyone causing Rugger trouble is likely to find a gang of hook-wielding men on their tail, all eager to help their Gram'ma out in any way they can.
hooks: Gram'ma has a job. One of her lodgers, Herr Bleanich, passed away in the night. She'd rather not deal with the Watch, so make the body go away and Gram'ma will owe you.
Gram'ma has another job. This one's a little bigger. Her husband, Karsten Rugger, is too scrupulous for her liking. She will be thankful if someone makes him vanish. Permanently.

locations.name: Strohmann Markt
locations.playerDescription: Strohmann Markt lies at the edge of the Teubrücke, where it connects to the fortified Precinct district. A relatively small, open square, it hosts a number of stalls by day, selling a wide variety of food and clothing. Hocheim's Livery Stables dominates one side of the platz, where visitors to Ubersreik can stable their horses. Next door to the stables, Marlies Zeitflug recently opened a small shop selling hourglasses and timepieces.
locations.gmNotes: Scarred and wrinkled Sabina Hocheim owns Hocheim's Livery Stables. An enterprising veteran of the last Parravon War, she spends her last days watching while her nephews and nieces do the work, intending for them to inherit the business. Marlies Zeitflug's shop is struggling in the current uncertain environment, and she is growing more concerned every day.
hooks: Hocheim has altered her will so her stables will be sold off on her death, the money being used to support soldiers' widows and children. Her nephew, Tilman, would rather she support her more immediate family. Should the party be able to produce a good forgery of the will, they will stand to profit, following Sabina's eventual demise.

Marlies Zeitflug needs some influential customers, in the hope that they may make her time-pieces more fashionable. Should the party be able to convince someone wealthy to buy a clock, they will earn a commission.

locations.name: Ubersreik Bridge & Dunkelfeucht
locations.playerDescription: Two centuries old, the Dwarf-built Ubersreik Bridge still dominates the city. It is supported by great, stone pillars sunk deep into the riverbed, rising to a height making it visible from much of the town. Local laws prohibit building atop the bridge, so those traversing it are greeted with fine views. Unseen from this vantage, a small shanty town known as Dunkelfeucht has sprung up under the bridge's shadow. The homeless and desperate gather here, and only the desperate now venture there.
locations.gmNotes: Gangs and footpads prowl Dunkelfeucht, and the Altdorf-led Watch avoids the place completely. This freedom from law-enforcement has allowed several makeshift jetties to be built by smuggling gangs. Recent rumours suggest the gangs are being bound together by a new leader known only as 'The Baron', a criminal mastermind known for his ambition and utter ruthlessness. The Baron is Katerine Eule, a woman from the rookeries of Altdorf who followed the army south to exploit the power vacuum.
hooks: The party have been hired by Klaus Osfer to locate his brother Ulli, who is somewhere in Dunkelfeucht. Ulli was kicked out of home by his father, who has now passed away, and Klaus wants him to come back. To get to him, the party will need to negotiate with The Baron, and her thugs.

Barrels of explosives have been reported stolen from the Miners' Guild, and the trail seems to lead to Dunkelfeucht. If the party investigate, they will discover the explosives are being stockpiled against some of the pillars of the bridge, with a view to destroying it. This plan is being orchestrated by Ernst Elsen, a destitute Human mason resentful of Dwarf influence on Ubersreik.

locations.name: Marktplatz
locations.playerDescription: Ubersreik's Marktplatz quarter stands at the heart of the town. Every Marktag (the weekly market day), farmers bring their produce from the surrounding villages to trade in the busy market squares, while pedlars and merchants display cloth and other produce. Most retailers within Ubersreik also pitch stalls on Marktag. At the centre of the Market Square, an imposing statue of Magnus the Pious stands, commemorating his pivotal role in rebuilding Ubersreik. The Marktplatz bustles with activity on most days, and is often used as a meeting point.

locations.name: The Physicians' Guild
locations.playerDescription: Across the square from the Temple of Shallya lies the Physicians' Guild, a modest but well-appointed building. Each of the town's three licensed physicians has an office and consultation room on the timber-and-lathe first floor, while the stone-walled ground floor contains a shared reception area and waiting room, and a thoroughly sound-proofed operating theatre.
locations.gmNotes: Doktor Otto Krupp is the eldest physician and Guildmaster; his principle concern is advertising his services, rather than patient care. Doktor Theodosia Grat is a bookish, driven graduate of the University of Altdorf, keen to learn as much as she can about illness and disease. Doktor Bernhardt Bayer is the youngest; charming and confident, he sees his profession as an opportunity to meet and impress the young men of Ubersreik.
hooks: Doktor Krupp is willing to pay a bounty of a shilling to anyone who can provide proof of a barber surgeon performing restricted work (such as the stitching of wounds) within the walls of Ubersreik. Of course, doing so would mean one's only future recourse for healing would be the Physicians' Guild, and their fees are steep.

Doktor Grat is a member of the Tinean Fellowship. Her obsession with diseases led to her worshipping Nurgle, the Chaos God of Disease. She has a secret shrine to the Plague Lord in the cupboard of her office, and has been injecting her patients with Bronze Fever to observe the effects.

locations.name: The Temple of Shallya
locations.playerDescription: The white walls of the Temple of Shallya, Goddess of Mercy, soar skywards near the Temple of Verena. It is a high-ceilinged building with a wide dome, all built in a classical style. Inside, there is an open space for worship and tending the sick. A series of curtained alcoves lie along both sides of the temple, where those with more severe or less dignified afflictions are placed. The inside of the dome is painted with a beautiful fresco of crying Shallya.
locations.gmNotes: Marianne Altenblum is the High Priestess, a matronly widow who joined the cult over a decade ago. She has a bottomless well of empathy, but no tolerance for flippancy or timewasters. She is assisted by a number of initiates and lay-members, who tend the sick and provide alms to the poor.
hooks: Altenbum has plans. She wishes to expand into the vacant building next to the temple, to create a hospice and infirmary for the town's poor. But to do so she will need donations and the blessing of the town's rulers. Any party able to secure either will find themselves in her good graces, and in receipt of free healing in perpetuity!

Esther Schultz, a dairy farmer, was taken ill last Marktag. High Priestess Altenblum would like the party to escort Esther home, so that she may die in peace. Unfortunately, Esther is dying due to exposure to warpstone. Over the course of the journey, she will gradually mutate. The horrors awaiting at her farm can only be imagined. And what about anyone who ate her cheese?

locations.name: The Temple of Verena
locations.playerDescription: The Temple of Verena, Goddess of Wisdom, stands at the south-east corner of Handel Square. A modest building, its services are attended regularly by scholars, including members of Ubersreik's judiciary. Behind the single-storey temple lies the 'Annexe', a large library open to all. The Annexe contains a broad, well-lit reading room and many cases of books and scrolls, including the town's charter and bylaws.
locations.gmNotes: The more valuable, or dangerous, books are located in a locked room, only accessible with the high priest's blessing. Heinrich Gutenberg is the high priest. A kindly man, with a long, flowing beard, Gutenberg believes knowledge is Verena's gift, and sees it as his sacred duty to share it. He is assisted by Dagmar Schirma, a shortsighted librarian who is clearly besotted with the high priest, a fact of which Gutenberg remains sadly ignorant.
hooks: After a theft from the Annexe, librarian Schirma asks the party to hunt down and bring back the books from various dealers and private collectors around town. She doesn't want Gutenberg to know, so won't involve the authorities. She will reimburse the party the cost of repurchasing the books plus a small amount. If the party can secure the books without paying, they could turn a profit.

Andreas von Bruner badly wants to read a restricted book, but Gutenberg refuses him. Anyone smuggling Andreas into the locked section will be paid handsomely. Of course, as he's secretly a cultist in thrall to the Chaos God Slaanesh, doing so may prove a very bad idea.

locations.name: Town Hall
locations.playerDescription: Ubersreik's Town Hall is an imposing stone building, two storeys high with four towers, that looms over the northern side of Marktplatz. In addition to banks of offices belonging to the Burgomeister and his staff, it contains the stately Nobles' Court, a grand hall in which the Jungfreud rulers historically made rulings. The towers were reserved for the Jungfreuds and visiting nobles to use as a residence but now lie unused.
locations.gmNotes: Since the removal of the Jungfreuds, the status and influence of the Town Council has risen dramatically. Ernst Maler is the current Burgomeister of Ubersreik and leader of the Town Council. His role was, until the arrival of Altdorf's troops, chiefly clerical. Given the potential for the town to become a Freiburg, things have changed — he is courted by Guildmasters and resented by the nobility loyal to the Jungfreuds.
hooks: Beneath the Town Hall, there is an old, disused gaol, with a half-dozen cells. Maler would like the cells cleared, 'as a precaution, only!'. Unbeknownst to Maler, a colony of giant spiders are nesting there, so clearing the basement will take more than merely moving boxes.

If the party have made contact with Maler, they will immediately come to the attention of the aspiring guildmasters, any of whom may contract the characters to lobby Maler on their behalf. Should different guilds coerce different party-members, the fallout could be messy...

locations.name: Sprichstumpf
locations.playerDescription: The Sprichstumpf is the stump of a great oak tree that once stood in what is now Market Square. It was felled during Magnus' reconstruction of the town. The remaining stump, which is around eight feet wide, stands not far from the statue of Magnus. It has become the focal point for the town's agitators and pamphleteers, an impromptu pulpit from whence they can rant and extort to the masses.
hooks: Anton Grimski, a firebrand agitator, has taken to visiting the Sprichstumpf most mornings, railing against the bourgeois corruption of Maler and the guilds. Grimski is, in truth, in the pay of the Jungfreuds, who wish to show the Burgomeister is unable to maintain order.

On Festag, a wandering Sigmarite mendicant begins to preach of the decadence of the Cult of Sigmar, drawing quite a crowd. The mood of the crowd begins to turn sour. A riot may erupt, unless the players take action.

locations.name: Theatre Varieté
locations.playerDescription: Originally a merchant's storehouse, this building was converted a decade ago into a proscenium arch theatre, which plays host to actors, musicians, and entertainers of all sorts. It is a large, stone building, with an expansive, vaulted, wooden ceiling. A large chalkboard hangs beneath the painted sign, on which the owner writes the name of the next performance. Inside, there are fifty seats in the stalls, another fifty in the upper circle, and two boxes reserved for the town's elite.
locations.gmNotes: Benedict Gurkenfeld, an actor and playwright of some renown, now runs the Theatre Varieté. During most days he can be found strolling around the Marktplatz observing the busking entertainers, scouting for talent. He has a number of stage-hands and ushers on staff, and directs a company of local amateurs who perform on occasion.
hooks: Disaster has struck. On the night of a sell-out performance, all of Gurkenfeld's performers have fallen ill after eating some dodgy shellfish. If the party have any skill at performing, this could be their big break.

Like all good theatres, the Theatre Varieté is haunted. The ghost is tormenting the visiting performers, and Gurkenfeld is desperate. Should the party investigate, they will discover that one of the stagehands, a Dwarf named Ragnar Torsson, has been faking the ghost in the hope of boosting ticket sales so he won't be fired.

locations.name: Watchstation
locations.playerDescription: This small building, not far from the Town Hall, is not more than four-foot across at its base. It has a heavy, oak door daubed with a crude rendition of the heraldry of Ubersreik. Inside, there is a waist-height metal pole against one wall with manacles attached.
locations.gmNotes: The Watch once used the Watchstation to hold drunks or to imprison criminals during night-time patrols. However, the keys to this and the other 11 Watchstations spread through Ubersreik, went missing during the Altdorf invasion.
hooks: Captain Pfeffer wants access to the Watchstations. She is advertising for any with the relevant skills to help her gain entry without causing damage so she can then replace the locks. However, the existing locks are Dwarf-wrought, and require a Very Hard (-30) Pick Lock Test. There is a reward of 2 GC on offer.
The Baron has the keys for the Watchstations, and is using them to store smuggled goods. She will not be happy should others gain access, and will seek vengeance if her contraband is taken.

locations.name: Merchant Quarter
locations.playerDescription: The Merchant Quarter extends eastwards from Marktplatz to the base of the Hill. It contains the Merchants' Guild, as well as a number of traders, retailers, and offices, as well as some smaller warehouses. Most of the buildings here are part stone, part timber, and even in these difficult times, several are being extended and redeveloped as trade in Ubersreik swells. By day, the quarter is usually busy, filled with burghers of all classes, but at night it grows quieter the further you stray from the Market Square, though it is well-patrolled by the Watch.

locations.name: The Dog Pens
locations.playerDescription: The Dog Pens is a wide square near the centre of the Merchant Quarter. It used to house kennels for dog fighting, but now hosts a number of middle-class eateries and taverns, including Frau Dehne's Tearoom and Sauer's Slophouse. The platz is popular amongst the burghers who live and work in the district, although it lies slightly off the beaten track.
locations.gmNotes: Frau Dehne runs her tearoom efficiently, selling no alcoholic beverages, but a range of hot brews and cold cordials, with cakes and pastries. In contrast, Sascha Sauer offers 'slop', a boiled down, congealed stew of vegetable tops and off-cuts of meat, which is tasty and nutritious, costing just 3d for a bowl and pint.
hooks: Perhaps the name 'The Dog Pens' is more accurate than many believe. Sauer frequently finds affordable meat hard to acquire, and will resort to unconventional sources when needs must. When the party, or a close ally, loses their small but vicious dog, they may not be consoled with a large portion of viscous slop.

Frau Dehne is a devout follower of Verena. After the death of her alcoholic husband, she came to believe that alcohol is the root of the Empire's current woes. She has started a temperance movement and asks the party to publicly abstain from drinking to help her garner support. She can't pay much money, but her raspberry cordial is to die for.

locations.name: The Exploding Pig
locations.playerDescription: Just off Abrechnungsplatz lies the Exploding Pig, a large tavern frequented by merchants, traders, and, on Marktags, visiting farmers. Its two floors are a hive of gossip, especially among local burghers with an interest in trade and local politics. Since the arrival of the State Soldiers from Altdorf, the Pig is much busier than usual as Ubersreik's chattering middle classes gather to discuss the latest developments.
locations.gmNotes: Hanno Rader, the landlord, named the inn after an accident in Dawihafen involving an abattoir and an armoury. He is as gossipy as a Nordlander fishwife and rarely gives others a moment to talk. He is also notorious as a reliable source of unreliable information. Rader's open support of the Burgomeister has earned him the disdain of locals loyal to the Jungfreuds.
hooks: While exiting at closing time, masked brigands attack the party and other patrons. If they decide to report the assault to the Watch, they realise that one of the assailants was Watch Sergeant Tirza Bronstein. He's quite prepared to lock up any with wild claims of corrupt watchmen.

Rader uses one of his private rooms upstairs to host a group of guildmasters who are consolidating their efforts to influence the Burgomeister. Kurt Prochnow, guildmaster of the Boatbuilders and Chandlers' Guild, will pay the party 1 GC to spy on the meeting and report back what they discover.

locations.name: Furlisdottir's Corn Exchange
locations.playerDescription: A large, two-storey, stone building, the Corn Exchange has been reconfigured as an indoor market, with numerous small retail stalls present on most days. The ground floor is a maze of stalls selling clothes, food, homewares, and knick-knacks of all kinds. A mezzanine gallery circles the building. More expensive items may be purchased there, and guards circulate to ensure customers don't try to lift stack without paying.
locations.gmNotes: Numerous traders offer their wares here, including: Ekkehard Eich, trader in rare books; Heinz Giegerich, a scribe who will read or write letters for a fee; and Malasa Nusa, an Arabyan textile merchant. The stallholders all pay rent to scowling Elke Furlisdottir, the Dwarf landlord. Elke's brother, 'Mighty' Borin Bozaksson, is responsible for security. Only the fastest or most foolish of thieves consider shoplifting under Borin's watch.
hooks: As the PCs browse the stalls, a worried merchant asks them to cover his stall while he nips to the privy. After half a bell, the real owner returns, wondering what happened to his good-for-nothing nephew and the day's takings.

Greta Klopstock, a young thief and initiate of the Crooked Fingers sect of the Cult of Ranald, is on her way out of the market, pursued by Borin. The party could intervene on either party's behalf, attempting to catch the thief in the hopes of a reward, or slowing the guard to ensure her escape in the hope of a future favour.

locations.name: Merchants' Guild
locations.playerDescription: The Merchants' Guild has become the political powerhouse of Ubersreik overnight. The guildhouse is currently a mass of wooden scaffolding, swarming with surly tradesmen, as it undergoes a series of renovations to ensure its facade reflects both civic pride and opulent wealth. There's a private club for local merchants on the ground floor. Upstairs there is a suite of more formal meeting rooms.
locations.gmNotes: Guildmaster Marta Müller is keen to exploit the guild's new influential force. Müller is a shrewd businesswoman with a jolly demeanour. Her family specialise in dairy products. She has been the master of the guild for three years, but the position is contested annually, drawing from representatives of the town's four main trading houses: Brauninger, Hertie, Karstadt, and Müller.
hooks: Müller is secretly a member of the Brotherhood, part of the Cult of Ranald. She is instrumental in moving funds from the cult's illicit activities in the Crooked Hammer to more legitimate ventures. If the party contains a Ranaldan, or have assisted the cult, she can smuggle them out of Ubersreik to Altdorf in a cheese barge.

Bengt Hertie, whose Merchant House trades in cloth and clothing, is very much the junior partner in the guild. He wishes to acquire gossip on his Brauninger, Karstadt, or Müller rivals, and will pay for any dirt. However, he's not the brightest man, and is easily fooled with any plausible 'secrets'.

locations.name: The Old Granary
locations.playerDescription: Dominating the skyline in the south of Ubersreik, the Old Granary is one of the fortress-town's tallest buildings. The conical construction is entirely built from stone, and has many doors up its north-facing side. It is wrapped with an external staircase that has seen better decades. It is currently the only granary within the town's walls.
locations.gmNotes: As flour is extremely flammable, the Old Granary is heavily guarded, and no naked flames, engineers, or wizards are permitted within ten feet by law. The Blessed Guild of Lady's Vale's Master Millers owns and maintains it. Flour is sold from a small kiosk; purchasers receive a clay chitty that can be redeemed at the Granary. The chitty set is changed daily to make it difficult for counterfeits. Ruprecht Adelmann is the guild's Ubersreik representative. He is often found after hours entertaining young men and women he picks up from local taverns.
hooks: The troops from Altdorf have come with their own supply of flour, which has driven down local prices and initiated a trade war. Should something happen to the Old Granary, it would devastate the local market, opening it up to importers. Marta Kroll, an Altdorfer merchant, is hoping this happens so she can trade with importers.

Adelmann's system of chitties is efficient and easy to counterfeit. The party is asked to acquire a chitty and deliver it to a fence in the Red Moon Inn. The 'Fence' is actually an agent of Captain Pfeffer of the Watch, on the lookout for a ring of counterfeiters. Quick-talking by the PCs might see them hired as her agents.

locations.name: Saint Bastian's Hospital
locations.playerDescription: Ubersreik's Merchants' Guild maintain this orphanage and school as a philanthropic gesture. It is a tall, narrow building in the Merchant Quarter. The ground floor contains a reception area, office space, a refectory and kitchens. The first floor contains classrooms and bathrooms, and the top floor contains the children's dormitory. Staff quarters are in the basement.
locations.gmNotes: Frederich Gewinnguter runs the Hospital, a charming middle-aged man who lives on site with his wife Hilde. During the day, additional staff attend, including Wolfram Weissman and Molrella Tüsch, who teach a broad curriculum to the children.
hooks: Mistress Tüsch wishes to take some of the children on a field trip into the Hagercrybs to observe the natural flora and fauna. Given rumours of bandits in the area, the Merchants' Guild are willing to pay for an escort. In fact, there are no bandits there, but the children are sure to provide trouble enough!

Unbeknownst to his employers, or his wife, Gewinnguter is a Daemonologist. In the evenings, he pores over his arcane grimoire, summoning lesser daemons. Despite dabbling in the dark arts, Gewinnguter is not yet in thrall to the ruinous powers, using the knowledge to blackmail a number of rivals. Gunther Grabbe, one of his victims, hires the party to investigate just how Gewinnguter gets his information.

locations.name: Sisters' Bakery
locations.playerDescription: A modest, stone built building, Sister's Bakery is tucked in between a leather shop and a milliner. It's a single storey, noticeably shorter than the other buildings on its street. Inside, there is a small area for serving customers, lined with shelves laden with bread and pies, with more delicate confections kept behind the counter. Most of the building's deep footprint is taken up by the bakery itself.
locations.gmNotes: Om and Nom Tumbleberry, twin Halfling sisters, run the bakery. They are identical and have a tendency to finish each other's sentences. They will happily interject into their customers' conversations. Om specialises in fine confectionery, while Nom is more experimental, and has recently been aping various Altdorf recipes, such as her popular lamprey pies.
hooks: Nom needs some very specific ingredients from Satrioli's Sausage Shop, but cannot buy them directly out of fear of the Lowhaven Clan. If the party can buy the ingredients without arousing suspicion, free pies all round!

The bakery is vandalised — the brick ovens hammered and the produce spoiled. When the short-staffed Watch take no interest, the Tumbleberrys turn to the party to investigate. If they follow the clues, they will discover a group of locals were riled up by Anton Grimski to target businesses fraternising with troops from Altdorf.

locations.name: Spirren-Hirsch and Gärtner
locations.playerDescription: Spirren-Hirsch and Gärtner are the foremost practitioners of law in Ubersreik. The timber and lathe office is currently being extended to allow for their growing number of clerks. The building is notable for its multiple entrances and exits, to allow discretion on the part of their clientele, particularly useful given the firm's propensity for representing both parties in civil cases.
locations.gmNotes: Wilhelm Gärtner and Melina Spirren-Hirsch are the firm's chief partners. Spirren-Hirsch is an intelligent, sophisticated woman in her 60s. Gärtner is only 30, with a brash, arrogant streak. Many student lawyers and clerks assist the partners.
hooks: In addition to their numerous street-front entrances, there is a secret entrance into the sewers, used by the firm's less savoury clientele. Bjorn Fellstren, a skittish racketeer, requires an escort, and the firm will pay well for the party to offer protection from sewer jacks, rats, or anything nastier.

Prosperity Lowhaven, a lawyer and representative of the Lowhaven Clan, is in litigation with one of Gärtner's clients. He will pay the party handsomely, if they can pose as clients, infiltrate Gärtner's office, and steal the relevant documents.

locations.name: Thulmannplatz
locations.playerDescription: A small square, Thulmannplatz is home to Ubersreik's stocks. In addition to criminals being punished by Magistrates, the Altdorf forces have taken to imprisoning anyone resisting their instructions, or publicly supporting the Jungfreuds. Sometimes these poor unfortunates remain locked up for hours, or even days. Ever enterprising, a number of Halfling stallholders have begun selling rotting fruit and vegetables to public-spirited Ubersreikers, which they can hurl at wrongdoers.
hooks: Genoveva Grün, an agitator who supports the expulsion of the Jungfreuds, has taken to riling crowds up. Sharp-eyed Characters may note that she is being paid in turn by the Halflings for increasing their trade. She is also employed by a crooked Sergeant in the Altdorf troops. When the party find themselves in his crosshairs, will this knowledge protect them?

When Severin Pfister, a visiting wool merchant, is arrested on trumped up charges, the crowd is so incensed that it swarms the stocks, intent on tearing him limb from limb. Will the party stand by and watch an innocent man be murdered? Will they step in and save him? Or join in, and loot his corpse?

locations.name: Unterdaumen Warehouses
locations.playerDescription: Seven small warehouses are ringfenced to the north of the Merchant's District and well-patrolled by private guards. They are owned by the Unterdaumen Merchant House. Each warehouse has large double-doors, is around ten-yards long, and has no windows.
locations.gmNotes: Grigerid Underdaumen is an octogenarian with a nose for profit. She is utterly ruthless, and enjoys nothing more than to destroy her rivals completely. She lives frugally in Underdaumen Warehouse VI, and has her favourite guard, Fritz Fritzman, wheel her to the Merchant Guild every morning.
hooks: Underdaumen deals with the Baron, the Lowhavens, Guido Falk, and several other criminal gangs. However, she doesn't want her guards caught up in obvious unlawful activity, so hires cheap outsiders to run errands and collect contraband.

Fritzman is a Yellowbelly who spies on criminal families for his masters. He reports to Slippery Jacob, a bawd from the Docks, and is overheard sharing Lowhaven secrets. They could be lucrative if sold to the correct party.

locations.name: Von Holzenauer's Potion Shop
locations.playerDescription: A spacious three-storey building, the Potion Shop has large arched windows illuminating the ground floor, where potions are made and sold. The first floor holds the spacious and well-lit private quarters of the owner, Siegfried von Holzenauer. The staff quarters lie above this, in the cramped attic rooms.
locations.gmNotes:
Siegfried von Holzenauer, a minor scion of a noble family, dabbles in potion-making as a hobby. He is far more interested in discovering and devising new recipes and sourcing rare ingredients than in turning a profit. As such, his staff will happily acquiesce to hagglers, offering potions at significantly discounted prices.

POTIONS FOR ALL SEASONS:
- Ameliorative Elixir (1/4): +10 WP, -10 Agi, Ini, Int. Duration 1d10x10 min.
- Focusing Philtre (5/-): +20 Int, End. Gain 1 Fatigued for a day after. Duration 1d10 hours.
- Liquor of Luck (1GC): +1 Fortune. On double d100 roll when spending Fortune, regain it. Lose all Fortune and gain 1 Fatigued after. Duration 1d10 min.
- Katya's Cordial (6/-): Gain Attractive Talent. Suffer -20 Fellowship for 1d10 days after. Duration 1d10 hours.
- The Marvellous Medicinal Mixture (8/-): Average(+20) Cool Test to drink. Gain 1 Fatigued. No other effect, but customers believe it works.
- Reactionary Restorative (1GC): Never gain Surprised Condition. Gain 1 Fatigued after. Duration 1d10 hours.
- Tonic of Sight Beyond Sight (10/-): Roll 1d10 for temporary Talent(s): 1-2: Acute Sense (Sight); 3-4: Holy Visions; 5-6: Magical Sense; 7-8: Second Sight; 9-10: all of the above. Duration 1d10 min.
hooks: Though von Holzenauer developed his Ameliorative Elixir as a painkiller, it is often used recreationally. The potion is almost absurdly cheap, and is sold at a markup in seedy establishments in the Docks. Viktoria Häussler, a bawd, will pay the party to purchase large quantities of the potion and bring them to her.

Gustavus Guggenheimer, a Wizard Lord of the Gold Order, is concerned that von Holzenauer's potions have unnatural effects. Given Holzenauer's noble status, Guggenheimer is reluctant to officially intervene, so has asked the party to investigate and determine what goes into the mysterious potions.

locations.name: Wahlund's Rat Catchers
locations.playerDescription: This guild is located in a former tavern on Grossweg. The tavern's sign had depicted a snarling, fat shark, so it now has a dead rat painted hastily into its mouth. The old taproom serves as a meeting room and clubhouse for the rat catchers and their visitors. The cellar houses a kennel for their dogs, and also contains a secure entrance into Ubersreik's sewer complex.
locations.gmNotes: Until recently, the rat catchers of Ubersreik barely had a guild. But then Wahlund, a foreign rat catcher, arrived with his 'Exterminators'. Wahlund bought an old inn, which he offered the guild if it let him lead them. The guild is lead by Guildmaster Wahlund, a scarred veteran Sewer Jack from the north. Unbeknownst to most, he is also a High Priest of Stromfels. He and his three compatriots are all that remain of a secret cult wiped out by a Skaven assault. They travel the Empire, slaughtering the ratmen, and seeking out Grey Seer Rasknitt, the architect of their cult's destruction. They have followed rumours of Rasknitt to Ubersreik and secreted a small shrine to Stromfels in the basement.
hooks: Wahlund wishes to hire the players to hunt rats, freeing him up to focus on hunting Skaven. Their discretion is appreciated and will be rewarded. Of course, once down there, it's likely they will inevitably encounter the four northerners on the hunt, and may well become embroiled in their secret quest for vengeance.

Thormo Hakenbein, one of the guild's most unassuming members, is secretly a Witch. With the guild's expansion, he fears discovery and will hire the party to investigate Wahlund and his friends, hoping that his coin will prevent them from looking into his own activities.

locations.name: Morgenseite (The Hill)
locations.playerDescription: Morgenseite, known locally as 'The Hill', is the most affluent quarter of Ubersreik. The homes of Ubersreik's wealthier middle-class families form a terrace leading up the Hill to the manors, mansions, and small estates of the wealthiest nobles, guildmasters, and clerics. Curving around the bottom of the Hill, Osterstrasse hosts the town's elite shops, including high-class couturiers, eateries, jewellers, armourers, and other luxury goods. The Watch patrol Morgenseite enthusiastically. Undesirables and those inappropriately dressed are likely to be moved along with a swift boot.

locations.name: Aschaffenberg Manor
locations.playerDescription: The Aschaffenberg residence is the second largest estate on the Hill. The striking two-storey manor has a coach-house and stables built into the north side, and a selection of out-buildings to the south, all of which are built in a classical style. It is officially the home of Duke Brynich of House Aschaffenberg and his wife, Duchess Eleanor.
locations.gmNotes: The uncertain future of Ubersreik has persuaded the duke to retire to his lands, leaving his wife to wrap up their affairs. However, Duchess Eleanor has no desire to leave her palatial residence and plans to do everything she can to never leave Ubersreik. Tancred Davieu is the head of staff and has been tasked with cataloguing and preparing the manor's contents for auction, work which is seriously impeded by Eleanor. Ten of the Duke's personal guard are garrisoned here.
hooks: In the chaos following the Duke's departure, Davieu's daughter, Krystal, pilfered some of the silver. Now the goods are to be sold in auction, and she needs to get the silver back to avoid suspicion. The silver is in a warehouse in the Docks belonging to Pip Shufflepig, a low ranking member of the Lowhaven Clan.

A shifty stranger claiming to be working for Duchess Aschaffenberg wants to hire the party to disrupt the impending auction, by stealing Davieu's list of goods. Entrance through the grounds should be relatively straightforward, there's just the matter of the Duke's guards to contend with.

locations.name: Brauninger House
locations.playerDescription: Owned by the Brauninger merchant family, this building is modest for The Hill. It contains 16 rooms, a large servants' quarters, and separate stables and coach house. The merchant house has contracts with several noble families and mercenary outfits across the Empire to supply arms: the family's primary business.
locations.gmNotes: Many of the town's forges are under the family's control, and the Metalworking Guild is a close ally. Sigmar Brauninger is a slight man in his early 50s. His house's business has grown impressively, with offices in Nuln, Altdorf, Carroburg, and Marienburg. This last acquisition may prove costly as the competition in that city is cut-throat.
hooks: Marius Strooper, a 'freelance consultant' from Marienburg, wants to hire a group to deliver a 'message' to Brauninger. The 'message' is to be secretly delivered directly into his office. Should his employees succeed, they will be ‘wealthy’. Should they fail, they may cause a diplomatic incident.

A shipment of Brauninger's arms is missing. Three wagons, containing blackpowder weapons, were en route from Nuln to Ubersreik. In the power vacuum, Brauninger was keen to secure a contract with the burgomeister to supply the Watch. He will pay generously for a party to hunt down his missing weapons and bring the culprits to justice.

locations.name: Emperor's Rest Hostel
locations.playerDescription: The six-storey Emperor's Rest sits at the base of the Hill by the northern end of the Osterstrasse and provides suites of rooms and fine dining for the wealthiest of Ubersreik. The prohibitive prices, and burly, if well-liveried, guards ensure the riff-raff are kept at bay. Political uncertainty has led to a drop in business, which concerns the staff.
locations.gmNotes: The fabulously wealthy Duke of Telland owns the impressive hostel. Managing the hostel on his behalf, the scrupulously clean Hedrich Hann monitors his 37 staff with a general's eye and a firm tongue. He's an especially devout man, and confesses to the priests of Sigmar in the High Temple every Festag.
hooks: Hann has a rodent problem. Should word of the rats in the basement get out, it could further affect trade, so he would like it taken care of quickly and quietly, which means no Ratcatchers' Guild. The evidence of the rats is clear to see, though the holes seem awfully large...

One of the characters recognises a customer staying at the Hostel. It's Mikhail Ziegel, a Charlatan, posing as a noble, and clearly planning something bigger. The party could reveal the truth, earning Hann's thanks. Or they could speak to Mikhail, and get in on his scam.

locations.name: Bruner Palace
locations.playerDescription: Von Bruners have lived on the site of Bruner Palace for centuries. The family is rich from its mines in the Hagercrybs, and it spends lavishly on the palace. It is the largest building on the Hill, with an impressive 239 rooms. It is in such a prominent position it can be seen from almost every part of the town. A large stables and coach house are built to the east end of the walled grounds, and a small jetty juts out into the Teufel at the foot of the Hill, where painted boathouses hold several pleasure barges.
locations.gmNotes: The estate is nominally controlled by Heinrich von Bruner, but in truth, his mother, Lady Kisaiya von Bruner, rules.
