Indomitable and authoritarian, she is currently raising three of her grandchildren: Andreas, Gutele, and Boniel. They hold lavish balls and salons that often last for days. Rumours of decadent pursuits persist, despite generous donations to the Cult of Sigmar.
hooks: The party are invited to the Palace, not realising they are the entertainment. Ordered to fight for their betters' amusements. Do they fight one another, in the hopes of securing funds and patronage, or do they try to fight their way out, past the von Bruners' guards?

Liesel Mair, an investigator, has been following up rumours of Andreas's corruption. She (rightly) believes he is part of a profane cult, planning some kind of unholy ritual. But nobody at the Watch will take her seriously. Will the party help her uncover a monster?

locations.name: Karstadt Estate
locations.playerDescription: House Karstadt, the richest merchant family of Ubersreik, owns this bustling, and continually expanding, estate. The fortified grounds are the third highest on the Hill. The main building has two floors containing a score or so rooms. Beside the manor is a stables and coach house with space for 24 horses and four coaches. Other buildings are spotted across the grounds, which also contain several copses of trees, ornamental ponds, and an impressive maze to amuse visiting guests.
locations.gmNotes: House Karstadt is known for trading in ores, metal, and luxury goods, running mines, and moneylending. Unknown to most, the Karstadts were formerly nobles of Ubersreik. Decades ago, Baron Victor Karstadt chose to surrender his nobility to secure a loan. The family fortunes have significantly changed for the better since. Hellin Karstadt-Stampf is the current head of the family. Her husband, Leuthold, rarely leaves their offices in Altdorf, leading to gossip that their marriage has broken down. Helping Hellin, Josef Specht, the purser, is never far from her side. An unassuming fellow, Specht is an almost invisible presence, yet is quickly on hand with a quill or a supply of coins.
hooks: Hellin's son, Alfred, yearns for a title to complement the wealth he will inherit. He is convinced the von Bruners retain his Grandfather's patents of nobility. He will richly reward anyone who will break into the Bruner Palace to retrieve them.

Hellin's daughter, Annika, has no interest in trade, longing instead to pursue a martial career. She will pay the party to train her in secret, hiring them to complete odd jobs around the estate to cover their furtive martial activities. But when Annika gets injured sparring, they will have to think fast.

locations.name: Luigi & Salvatore
locations.playerDescription: Luigi & Salvatore is where the wealthy and indulgent of Ubersreik shop. It is a dark granite, three-storey building faced with large windows. Within, shoppers encounter a labyrinthine tangle of columns and shelves with dozens of attendants ready to help customers, or eject time-wasters and riff-raff. All manner of high quality, high priced goods can be purchased here: clothing, arms and armour, supplies, writing materials, and so much more.
locations.gmNotes: Adriana Corolla manages the opulent shop. She spends most of her time dealing with paperwork in her office in the basement. She will personally serve her most influential clientele, and takes regular breaks to stride the shopfloor, making loud, supportive comments in her distinctive Tilean accent.
hooks: The party are hired by Corolla to act as mystery shoppers. She believes one of her attendants, Tamara, is skimming. The party are given 20 silver shillings to spend, on the proviso that they catch Tamara in the act.

To ingratiate themselves with Silvi Kreutzhame, Priestess of Ranald, the party must each steal an item of value from the store and donate it to the poor. The item must be of use, and the theft must go unnoticed.

locations.name: Wings of the Pegasus
locations.playerDescription: The Wings of the Pegasus is the finest eatery in Ubersreik, and, so its owners claim, all of Reikland. It sits near the top of Osterstrasse, with a commanding view of the town spread below it. Customers willing to pay their exorbitant rates are treated to food that is both exotic and subtly cooked. They often serve selections from rare and exotic animals and monsters. There is a small private dining room and balcony on the first floor.
locations.gmNotes: Johann Zustrass is the head chef, assisted by a team of Halfling sous-chefs. Zustrass is as legendary for his fiery temper, as for his varied menu. Maître d' Laurent Bonappetit manages the front of house staff. Bonappetit is a reed-thin Bretonnian with a wispy moustache and oily manners.
hooks: Zustrass is about to entertain an influential customer, but he lacks a key ingredient: Manticore liver. His normal supplier is away. Zustrass has a map and a wagon, and will pay the party to fetch a fresh Manticore corpse.

Bonappetit is a fraud. He is really Dante Blau, a charlatan. He is trying to stay out of crime, but a noble lord he once conned has a reservation for this evening. He has to work, so he is offering the party a free meal in exchange for them running interference, with one of them masquerading as Bonappetit while serving the lord in the private dining room.

locations.name: Madame Beaumarteau's
locations.playerDescription: The stone facade of this long, low shop is carved with the shapes of traditional masks. The carving is beautifully wrought, making the shop stand out. Madame Beaumarteau's is the premiere boutique for an array of fine costumes as well as fancy masks and more austere garb.
locations.gmNotes: Madame Beaumarteau is an aging spinster, stout of limb and heart. She sews much of her work herself, but employs a gaggle of Halfling seamstresses to assist her. Despite her stern demeanour, she is a kind soul, and will often offer reduced prices to less well-off clients, while overcharging those who are arrogant and abrasive.
hooks: One of Beaumarteau's seamstresses, Lolly Skelfsider, has gone missing. Madame Beaumarteau believes the Lowhavens have kidnapped her and are holding her in Satrioli's Sausage Shop. She will pay the party to return her, but the truth is that Lolly is in love with Sunny Lowhaven and has recently eloped with him. The Lowhavens are not happy.

Given her position in society, Madam Beaumarteau is privy to all manner of secret intelligence. When the Characters pay a visit, they find the owner missing and her staff in disarray. They believe a gang of brigands have kidnapped her, looking to extort information from her. They left no clues, though the door looks like it was forced with some kind of curved metal blade, like a boot hook.

locations.name: Auld Odenhaus Pantera
locations.playerDescription: Built in 1589 IC by the Knights Panther — a wealthy order of secular knights — this chapterhouse is a small, opulent building on the Hill. Stairs lead to an upper floor of grand chambers, including a smoky club house and library. Beneath lies an ornate stable, training square, and servant halls. For all its splendour, the building is crooked, sagging, and alarmingly creaky.
locations.gmNotes: No Knights Panther permanently lodge there, and it's rare for more than five to be in residence. Chamberlain Adella Markel leads the Odenhaus's 6 staff and 13 guards. All wear blue livery with a snarling panther on their chest.
hooks: Man-at-arms Helrella Markel has waited all her 53 years to be Chamberlain, and will wait no longer. She needs a group willing to murder a 76 year-old grandmother, and will pay well. But she won't mention Adella trained with Knights Panther all her life, and is likely the finest swordswoman in Ubersreik.

Knight-Captain Brander von Gerlbach of the Knights Panther is deeply suspicious of the motivations behind the seizure of Ubersreik, and has arrived to investigate. He works from the Odenhaus, and is looking for alert mercenaries to help him.

locations.name: The Precinct
locations.playerDescription: The Precinct is Ubersreik's military district, centred around the fortress of Magnus's Tower. It was built using some of the foundations of the town from before it was razed. It is separated from the rest of Ubersreik by stout walls. Though the gates are rarely closed, in cases of civil unrest, they can be used to turn the district into a defacto fortress. In simpler times, the State Army, the Watch, and provincial guards were stationed here.
locations.gmNotes: Since the arrival of the troops from Altdorf, tensions have noticeably escalated. The uncertainty regarding jurisdiction has led to clashes between the local troops and the interlopers, resulting in fighting in the streets. While there have been no deaths as yet, commanding officers fear it is only a matter of time before one side or the other takes things too far.

locations.name: Chapel of Ulric
locations.playerDescription: Though called the Chapel of Ulric, it is actually a temple. It is a large, cold building with an imposing stone façade — resembling a fortress more than a temple. Within, a flame burns day and night, beside a large statue of a grim-faced Ulric. The intense concentration of military folk in Ubersreik means this temple is more frequently attended than might be expected.
locations.gmNotes: Denfather Holst Kretschmer, a heavily bearded Middenlander, tends the temple. In addition to two other priests, Kretschmer has a small contingent of Knights of the White Wolf stationed in the temple. Mostly older, they all bear some injury, but they are fearsome fighters, meaning the temple has been spared the worst of the recent troubles, ironically making it one of the calmest places in town.
hooks: Captain Steyer, an Altdorfer, believes that Father Kretschmer has been assisting the local troops. Keen to discredit the Ulricans, he wants the party to enter the temple and douse the flame that burns within. Doing so is a blasphemous insult, and one the temple's knights are unlikely to take kindly to.

Brother Yannik, a young priest of Ulric, is not especially devout. At a recent conclave, he encountered Sister Gabriela Brestrich, a Shallyan initiate. He tells the party that they have fallen deeply in love and now plan to elope. Should the party help, they may be surprised to discover she is unaware of his existence.

locations.name: Magnus's Tower
locations.playerDescription: Magnus's Tower is an imposing building, a tall spire surrounded by sturdy walls, a fortress at the heart of The Precinct. The tallest structure in Ubersreik, it has a commanding view of the surrounding countryside and dominates the town's skyline. Access to the tower is gained through a complex series of Dwarf-engineered elevators, powered by cunning use of counterweights and levers.
locations.gmNotes: The Tower is the only military position not controlled by the Altdorf State Army, and is instead manned by local soldiers who have disavowed the Jungfreuds. Captain Erwin Blucher commands the troops. He is 'advised' by Field Marshall Antonin Sieber, an aged veteran whose wits have largely fled. Sieber's honour guard comprises a small detachment of Reiksguard Knights from Altdorf.
hooks: The Reiksguard are in a unique position to ease tensions. Captain Preis, their de facto leader, is keen to do so, but cannot act without the Field Marshal's explicit authorisation, and he will not listen to her. However, it so happens he served with one of the Characters' grandfathers, and is keen to reminisce. Perhaps they can convince him?

Blucher is an arch-opportunist. While most of his men still secretly support the ousted Graf Sigismund, he is enjoying his freedom. He is keen to ensure Ubersreik becomes a strong, independent Freiburg. If Blucher is seen meeting with the Burgomeister, there will be mutiny, so he needs the party to smuggle him to the Town Hall.

locations.name: The Mess and Bucket
locations.playerDescription: The Mess and Bucket is an inn that caters almost exclusively to the soldiery of Ubersreik. It has a large common room that is technically open to the public, although civilian patrons will draw disapproving scowls and jeers. The furniture is cheap, given how regularly it is broken in bar fights. Upstairs, the inn offers a private club, with membership available to officers. Access is via an external staircase.
locations.gmNotes: Otto 'Cabbage' Klemp is head bouncer, a retired Sergeant. Dietmar Varttiger is the maître d' of the private First Floor Club, a supercilious, oily fellow. Berthold 'Big Bert' Hanson tends bar downstairs and is the owner of the establishment.
hooks: Tensions in the Club have been strained after the Altdorfers arrived. When Lieutenant Eisner, an officer in an Altdorf handgunner regiment, seemingly breaks his neck falling down the stairs, Varttiger employs the party to tidy things up, without involving Cabbage, or the Watch.
Cabbage is always on the lookout for strong arms and brave hearts. PCs short on cash could work a few shifts breaking up brawling infantrymen, assuming they don't mind losing a few teeth.

locations.name: North Temple of Sigmar
locations.playerDescription: The North Temple of Sigmar is functional, without clever carvings or glittering icons. It is most commonly frequented by soldiers and non-commissioned officers. The higher ranks favour the High Temple, and the social and political opportunities it confers.
locations.gmNotes: The high priestess in residence, Mother Dörflinger, lost her arm fighting Greenskins in the Grey Mountains. She was later stationed in Ubersreik to train the town's militia. Since the arrival of the forces from Altdorf, attendance at her weekly throngs and training sessions has significantly increased.
hooks: Disgruntled locals are using the militia drills to train for an assault against the invading forces from Altdorf. Wise to this, General von Dabernick sends his men to infiltrate. When the party attend the temple, sparks fly.
News of Goblin attacks in nearby villages concerns Mother Dörflinger. She believes Skarrik, the Wolfrider that took her arm, leads the raids. She needs help and vengeance.

locations.name: Reiniger's Outfitters
locations.playerDescription: Reiniger's has been the principal outfitters for Ubersreik's military forces for decades. A large, two-storey building, it bears an air of genteel charm at odds with its surroundings. The ground floor services rank and file uniforms, with a small office and the bulk of the space used for storage and for a small army of seamstresses. The first floor is reserved for Officers, where they can have their measurements taken.
locations.gmNotes: Florian Reiniger is the chief tailor, with a relaxed and easy manner. He is skilled at stitching and at talking his customers into buying an extra jacket.
hooks: Florian is working for High Lord Holzgrug, the Imperial Spymaster. It was his intelligence that allowed Altdorf to take the town so quickly. Olla Olwin, a former colleague, knows Florian's secret. Olla is languishing in the cells at the Watch Barracks, and Florian needs the PCs to infiltrate the cells and eliminate the threat.

Reiniger's assistant, Herr Katz, has a secret. Reiniger rescued Katz from slavery over twenty years ago. His former owner, Mario Malpensi, has a long memory and deep pockets. He has an agent, Davide Avido, in town, who will approach the PCs, seeking their assistance in returning Katz to captivity. The reward is great, but slavery is illegal in the Empire.

locations.name: Ubersreik 3rd Barracks
locations.playerDescription: This sizeable barracks once billeted Ubersreik 3rd Regiment of Foot, the Reikland 33rd, nicknamed: 'the Fighting Stags'. The regiment retreated as the State Army of Altdorf approached, so the building now lies empty. A large wall rings the muster ground where the soldiers once drilled. Against the wall are towers, workshops, barracks, kitchens, refectories, and chapels, most of which are locked and quiet.
locations.gmNotes: Aware the barracks may become a rallying point for Jungfreud sympathies, General von Dabernick ordered the walls patrolled with Altdorf soldiers. At any one time, two squads of eight halberdiers march around the periphery. Sergeant Rikard Jaekel is making the best he can of the barracks. He's managed to requisition several barrels of ale. Since the nearby chapels are locked, he's built a small shrine to Ranald and another to Ulric in the north tower.
hooks: The banner of the Fighting Stags hangs in the main refectory. Gunner Wictor Franko recently arrived from the duchy of Black Rock intending to reclaim it for his regiment. However, he didn't expect security in his old barracks to be so high, so he's looking for help, or just a simple distraction...

Rikard really misses his pregnant wife, Hanna. She works in a Ranaldan gambling den in Altdorf. Should Rikard die, he will not go quietly, and will persistently haunt any responsible until certain his wife is safe.

locations.name: Watch Barracks
locations.playerDescription: The Watch barracks include a number of offices, an array of holding cells, and basic quarters. The Watch regularly patrol the town in groups ranging from two to six. While their patrols should cover the entire town outside Black Rock, in practice they concentrate on wealthier areas, seldom venturing far into the Docks or the Dunkelfeucht.
locations.gmNotes: The bulk of the old Watch members were recently dismissed due to suspicion they were loyal to the von Jungfreuds. So, much of the current Watch is made up of Altdorf soldiers who've been pressed into service, and who resent it. They have little interest in justice and swiftly resort to busting heads to keep order. Captain Andrea Pfeffer commands the Watch. She is a no-nonsense woman in her 20s. The newly appointed Captain is concerned with the disruptions and is keen for the Burgomeister's position to be consolidated, or a new noble family installed.
hooks: Captain Pfeffer believes one of her watch sergeants, Trudi Shrieber, is on the pay of the Lowhaven Clan of Halflings. Unable to trust her Watch, she enlists the party to follow Shrieber and secure evidence of her wrongdoing.

When resolving a bar fight in The Exploding Pig, older members of the Watch want to arrest an off-duty Altdorfer, while his comrades, along with some 'newer' watch members, want him set free. The PCs stumble into this tense standoff...

locations.name: The Sewers
locations.playerDescription: Ubersreik's sewers are extensive and a source of local pride. Two distinct networks exist: one to the city's north (the Magnussewers), and another to the south (the Sigmarsewers). Both networks discharge into the Teufel through wide, steel-grated culverts. Each network comprises around a dozen major, arterial sewers, through which a four-foot wide effluent channel flows, flanked by equally wide walkways. Smaller tunnels connect these arterial sewers. Vaulted chambers, twenty-feet across, sit at the junctions. Intricate carvings of Dwarf faces line the chambers' columns, though few consider the splendid sight worth the appalling reek.
locations.gmNotes: When Greenskins razed the town 200 years ago, the sewers were untouched. Later, Empire infiltrators, led by Dwarf scouts, entered the town through the sewer grates to surprise the occupying Greenskin forces. This story is well known locally, but the invading Altdorfers have no idea. The southern network (Sigmarsewers) is better maintained. Nonetheless, there have been numerous sightings of fast-moving Beastmen with ratlike visages. The northern network (Magnussewers) is less regularly patrolled and, in addition to the omnipresent threat of ratmen, other creatures call the sewers home, such as Skaven Gutter Runners, Giant Rat Swarms, and a Doppelganger named Brandt.

locations.name: Fleshmarket
locations.playerDescription: The Ubersreik fleshmarket lies to the north-east of the town. Given the law against stone buildings near the walls, it comprises a handful of wooden buildings, with a number of stakes forming pens alongside pitches for tents and wagons, including a stables and a kennel which are permanent fixtures. Other beasts (pigs, cattle, sheep, and similar) are driven to the pens on a rotational basis.
locations.gmNotes: Juna Sattelrücken is Ubersreik's main horse-coper. A wiry Averlander in her 30s, she drives a hard bargain, but a fair one, and treats her horses kindly. On the other hand, Stanislaus Stockman, the hundsman, is a brute. In his 40s, he is handsome and tall, but his glittering eyes betray the cold heart lying within. He believes in discipline, and is not above beating his dogs, employees, and anyone else.
hooks: On their way to Ubersreik, the party meet a downhearted farmer, Jan Boehm, whose precious pigs were stolen by bandits. When they arrive, they see the pigs have already been sold to Sartioli's Sausage Shop. All they need to do is ask the Halfling crime family who sold them their pigs, and hope they weren't in on the theft.

Juna Sattelrücken has heard there are wild horses, of good Bretonnian stock, loose in the foothills of the Grey Mountains. She needs an escort to accompany her as she tries to capture them. Unfortunately, there are monsters out there, but she can pay, or offer a good deal on a steed...

locations.name: Morr's Field
locations.playerDescription: To the northwest of Ubersreik lies the town's graveyard, Morr's Field. It is surrounded by tall and crumbling stone walls. Within lie the graves and ravenstones of Ubersreik. Mass graves for paupers, single plots for the middle-classes, and great mausoleums for the wealthiest families in town. Additionally, there is a shrine to Morr, which is attached to a larger hall, used by the Mourners' Society, an informal group of locals who offer solace to the grieving.
locations.gmNotes: Schadrach Bürke is the ranking priest of Morr, the God of Death. Bürke is a tall, angular man with a long nose and a mournful aspect. He rarely leaves the Field, and has little Human contact, save when comforting those who have lost loved ones, or issuing instructions to his two gravediggers, Ewald and Oswald.
hooks: Holst Rosenstock is a graverobber and a drunk. Having recently incapacitated himself by falling into the jakes of the Crooked Hammer, he is unable to fulfil a contract and owes Doktor Krupp a body. Holst will pay the party over the odds (up to 2 GC each) to do the job for him in order to preserve his reputation.

Father Bürke has noticed someone or something disturbing the graves, and he would like to pay the party to deal with it. If they accept, and are brave enough to spend the night, they will discover a group of Ghouls that have been feasting on the dead.

locations.name: The Tin Spur
locations.playerDescription: The Tin Spur is a large, open-roofed, circular building near the southern Nuln Gate. It is used for various entertainments, including bear-baiting, dog fights, and pitfighting. It is occasionally used by entertainers to put on plays. The building lies outside the town's walls, owing to a bylaw put in place because the sight of blood offended Lady Jungfreud. There are three floors of galleries for watching the performances. A series of pens lie attached to the rear.
locations.gmNotes: The Esteemed Company of Ubersreik Players own and maintain the building. Chief among them is their playwright, Wilhelm Shütteln, whose works tend to be overlong and wordy. Nonetheless, as the chief stakeholder in the company, he chooses the plays performed. It is a source of constant frustration for Shütteln that animal and pit fights always make significantly more money, meaning he performs but rarely.
hooks: The Lowhaven Clan of Halflings plan to run their own pitfights in the Docks, but need a main attraction. As such, they're willing to pay the party to get Felix Seite, The Tin Spur's champion, drunk, before kidnapping him and taking him to their warehouse.

Ubersreik's Animals Front (UAF) is an active group of concerned citizens led by a Shallyan initiate, Konstance Pfleger. They plan to sneak backstage during one of Shütteln's interminable plays and set all the animals free. As the members of UAF lack any real physical skills, they have hired the party to assist.

locations.name: The Red Moon Inn
locations.playerDescription: The two-storey Red Moon Inn primarily caters to boatmen plying their trade up and down the Teufel. It’s the cleanest of the dock-side hostels, though still somewhat shabby. The lower floor is built from solid stone and includes a large drinking hall, common room, and small kitchen. The upper floor is timber and lathe and contains the inn’s private rooms, and a room for the owner. The main drinking hall has a row of quiet booths all slung with heavy curtains and tattered linen to provide a little privacy.
locations.gmNotes: Franz Lohner owns and runs the inn. A no-nonsense Mercenary done-good, Lohner is a slightly overweight, dishevelled man in his 40s. He employs Ilse Frecht, a matronly woman in her 50s, to clean rooms and wait tables. Gunter Bisset works in the kitchens, cooking dinner, and two younger lads to help serve during busier times. All Bisset ever produces is potato and fish stew. A wholesome meal, but one that doesn’t make the best breakfast in the morning when served as cold leftovers.
hooks: While enjoying a tasty stew, the party overhear plans to allow brigands in through the town gates at midnight. One of the conspirators is in the Watch, but they didn’t get a clear view of him, and without proof, the authorities will never believe them. The watchman had a distinctive voice, though. Have they got time to talk to all the watchmen in Ubersreik before nightfall?

As the party are celebrating being paid by settling in to a round of good, strong beers, two masked hoodlums enter the Inn, bearing loaded pistols. Kürbis and Honighäschen, a pair of legendary married brigands, urge everyone to stay calm and hand over all their wealth. Honighäschen warns that should anyone move, she will execute every last patron in the inn.

locations.name: The Axe and Hammer
locations.playerDescription: The Axe and Hammer is the only dedicated tavern in Dawihafen, though there are also three inns. The Axe and Hammer has one floor above ground, containing a large common room and a number of smaller booths and meeting rooms. The walls, floors, tables, and chairs are all made of stone, and intricately wrought with images of Dwarf ancestors. The ceilings are low, and the building has no windows, being lit by lamps and a great fire roaring in the centre of the large open space. Although most customers are Dwarfs, all folk are welcome.
locations.gmNotes: The basement level of the inn is for Dwarfs only, and it resembles the great hall of a Dwarf hold. It contains shrines to Grungni and Valaya — two Dwarf ancestor Gods. It is also the site of the Dwarf Engineers’ Guild in town. Grodni Surehammer, a longbeard, leads this august institution. He answered Magnus’s call for aid centuries ago, and has remained in Ubersreik ever since. He is the de facto leader of the Dwarf community in Ubersreik. Visiting Dwarfs consider it a great honour to meet Surehammer, and often frequent the inn just to shake his hand.
hooks: Tunnels connect the tavern to the Khazalgirt, and from thence to the homes of a number of prominent Dwarfs. In pursuit of a Skaven menace, the Characters find themselves blundering into the basement, bringing them face to face with a group of irate Dwarfs convinced they are raiding the inn!

Ivar Broadthumb, a Dwarf metalworker, is enraptured by Dordean Mournflair, the Elf behind the Cutlers’ Guild. He wants to meet the secretive smith to discuss methodology, in defiance of traditional Dwarf attitudes to metalworking, and Elves. He needs the party to convey a message, secretly, and arrange a secure, private, neutral space for the meeting, if they can convince Mournflair to come

locations.name: Wizards' Way
locations.playerDescription: Graf Otto Strasse is a long, winding street that snakes through the eastern end of the Artisan Quarter. It is known colloquially as Wizard’s Way, as it is home to the town’s only permanent wizard. The street mostly comprises small shops selling herbs, books, and other esoterica, but it is dominated by the Grey Wizard’s tower — a crooked, slate-roofed turret — that peeps above the other stone and timber buildings. Although the tower can be clearly seen, its actual entrance is seemingly impossible to locate. Curious visitors have circumnavigated the tower repeatedly in search of a door or alleyway, but to no avail; locals gave up long ago.
locations.gmNotes: Grey Guardian Christoph Engel has called Ubersreik his home for as long as anyone can remember. He is a wiry, unassuming fellow with dark-grey eyes and a neatly trimmed grey beard. On official business, he tends to dress formally, in flowing grey robes, with a pointed, wide-brimmed hat and a staff. However, when seeking to pass incognito, he favours the nondescript clothing of a burgher, the better to blend in and avoid a scene.
hooks: Engel is often bored with the responsibilities of his rank. He is not above quietly misusing his magic to create minor illusions to trick and disturb citizens for his own amusement. If he hears one of the party disparage wizards while out and about in disguise, he determines to make the party the butt of his jokes until they repent.

A coalition of local burghers, concerned at plummeting property prices on the Wizard’s Way, have clubbed together to pay a Witch Hunter to obtain proof of Engel’s misuse of magic, and have him evicted (or burned). The Witch Hunter, Mattheus Hüpfen, is not above framing his targets. He has decided to hire some local muscle to help him confront the wizard.

locations.name: The High Temple of Sigmar
locations.playerDescription: The High Temple of Sigmar, the Empire’s patron god, was the first building rebuilt on the orders of Magnus the Pious after the old one was levelled by Greenskins during the Great War Against Chaos. It is the largest temple in town, dwarfing those in other quarters. The facade is lined with pillars, and the temple itself can hold hundreds of worshippers.
locations.gmNotes: On especially busy Festags (festival days), poorer worshippers huddle outside the doors, straining to hear the service. Recently, locals have found the temple significantly busier, as it is filled with officers and soldiers from Altdorf. Father Gunther Emming is the High Priest. A stern looking man in his 50s with thinning silver hair, Emming is famed for the severity of his sermons, and the sobriety of his demeanour. Though not unkind, he laces even his praise and comforting words with dire warnings of the consequences of vice.
hooks: Irma Brantl, a pious if somewhat naive, young priestess of Sigmar has recently arrived in Ubersreik. Father Emming finds her gentle nature and incessant blithe chat incompatible with his view of the world. He is seeking ways to keep her out of his hair. He will pay the party well to escort her on a tour of the surrounding villages, to meet with the priests there. He will pay double if they take their time. Two or three months should do…

Dark dreams haunt those who spend too much time in the basement. Recently a farmer’s child disappeared on Marktag. TThe clues seem to suggest it was taken to the temple of Sigmar. Ernst Ricker, of the Order of the Cleansing Flame, is the only person with rooms in the basement of the temple. He may have lost his mind to the Ruinous Powers, but who is righteous enough to accuse him of heresy?

locations.name: Gravediggers
locations.playerDescription: Next to Morr's Field lies the modest home of Ubersreik's gravediggers, Ewald and Oswald. The two brothers live a simple life, rising early to tend to their duties in the graveyard. Their home is a small, stone cottage with a thatched roof, surrounded by a modest garden where they grow vegetables and herbs. Inside, the cottage is sparsely furnished but clean and orderly, reflecting the brothers' practical nature.
locations.gmNotes: Ewald and Oswald are quiet, unassuming men in their late 40s. They have worked as gravediggers for most of their lives, and take great pride in their work. Despite the morbid nature of their profession, they are kind-hearted and respectful individuals who treat the dead with dignity. They are well-known in the community and are often sought out for their knowledge of local history and customs related to death and burial.
hooks: Ewald has recently discovered a hidden chamber beneath Morr's Field, filled with ancient relics and inscriptions. He believes these artifacts hold significant historical value and wishes to share them with a reputable scholar. However, he fears that the local authorities may not take kindly to his discovery. He seeks the party's assistance in safely transporting the relics to Altdorf for study.

Oswald has been plagued by strange visions and nightmares since the arrival of the Altdorf soldiers in Ubersreik. He believes that a restless spirit is haunting him, seeking justice for an unresolved crime. Desperate for relief, he turns to the party for help in uncovering the truth behind the spirit's unrest and putting it to rest.

locations.name: Elise's Exquisites
locations.playerDescription: Just outside the northern Magnus the Pious Gate stands a small, crooked cottage with a sign depicting a smiling porcelain doll. The shop, 'Elise's Exquisites', is a riot of colour and form. Dolls of every conceivable size and material — wood, cloth, porcelain, wax — are crammed onto shelves, hang from the ceiling on strings, and stare out from the dusty shop window with unnervingly lifelike glass eyes.
locations.gmNotes: The shop is run by Elise Schmidt, a hunched old woman with a deceptively sweet smile and nimble, spidery fingers. She is a delight to talk to, especially for children. In truth, Elise is a hedge-necromancer who binds the spirits of the recently deceased into her creations. She doesn't see it as evil, merely 'giving them a bit more time in the sun.' The most expensive dolls are eerily realistic because they incorporate real hair, teeth, and fingernails sourced from the gravediggers at Morr's Field.
hooks: A wealthy merchant's daughter received a beautiful custom-made doll from Elise a week ago and has since been struck by a terrible wasting sickness. The doll has been heard whispering to the child at night. The merchant will pay anything to have the 'curse' investigated and lifted.

While passing the shop, one of the party members spots a brand new doll in the window that is a perfect, uncanny replica of themselves, right down to a specific scar or piece of equipment. Elise just smiles and says 'a little inspiration struck,' but will not say where she got the idea... or the materials.

locations.name: Eisbog Brewery
locations.playerDescription: South of the city, amidst the rolling farmland, stands the Eisbog Brewery. It's a large complex of stone and timber buildings, constantly venting clouds of steam that smell of boiling grain and hops. The brewery is famous for 'Eisbog Lager,' a potent beer known for being served unnaturally cold, even in the height of summer. A taproom attached to the main building serves the brew straight from the source, and is popular with off-duty soldiers and farmers.
locations.gmNotes: The brewery is run by Gunther Eisbog, a large, bearded man with a booming laugh. The Eisbogs are an old family, and their brewing secret is a source of immense pride. The secret is a fist-sized chunk of glowing green rock — warpstone — that Gunther's grandfather found in a crater. It's kept in a lead-lined net and lowered into the main fermentation tank to chill the brew. The family is ignorant of its true nature. The prolonged, low-level exposure is what gives the beer its 'kick,' but it is also slowly corrupting the brewery's most loyal patrons.
hooks: The brewery's long-time bouncer, a massive fellow named 'Stomper' Hans, has gone berserk in the taproom, babbling about 'the icy voice in the beer' before sprouting a tentacle from his shoulder. Gunther Eisbog needs the situation 'handled' before the Watch gets involved and starts asking questions.

Borgun Foambeard, the Dwarf brewer in Dawihafen, is losing business to the popular Eisbog Lager. Convinced no human could brew such a fine, cold beer without cheating, he hires the party to infiltrate the brewery and discover the Eisbog family's secret.

locations.name: Little Teufel Outpost
locations.playerDescription: West of the city, where the smaller Teufelia river flows into the mighty Teufel, stands a fortified toll-station known as the Little Teufel Outpost. Consisting of a sturdy stone watchtower, a ferryman's hut, and a small jetty, it controls both river traffic and the ferry crossing. The post is manned by a handful of grizzled Riverwardens, their livery faded and worn.
locations.gmNotes: The outpost is commanded by Warden Hella Stark, a pragmatic and world-weary woman in her forties. Officially, she serves the state, collecting tolls and inspecting cargo. Unofficially, the outpost is a major chokepoint for smugglers, and Warden Stark gets a cut of everything that passes. She walks a tightrope, placating the Lowhaven Clan who use her services, while filing just enough reports to keep the newly-installed Altdorf authorities from looking too closely.
hooks: The party is hired to smuggle a cargo of Bretonnian brandy. When they reach the rendezvous point, their contact turns out to be Warden Stark herself. She needs an independent crew to move a 'special shipment' under the noses of both her own guards and a Lowhaven agent who is watching her.

An ambitious junior officer from the Altdorf garrison, Lieutenant Kettner, suspects the outpost is a nest of corruption. Lacking the authority to launch a formal investigation, he hires the party as 'concerned citizens' to travel to the outpost and find concrete proof of Stark's illegal activities.

locations.name: Fronich Woodcutters Company
locations.playerDescription: Deep in the forests west of Ubersreik lies the sprawling lumber camp of the Fronich Woodcutters Company. The air is filled with the rhythmic thud of axes and the scent of pine sap and sawdust. Dozens of rough-looking men and women work felling trees and processing lumber, their temporary settlement a muddy collection of huts, tents, and a large cookhouse.
locations.gmNotes: The camp is run by the grizzled and grim-faced Old Man Fronich. The recent coal shortage has been a boon for business, but it has forced his crews to push deeper into the forest than ever before. In doing so, they have encroached upon the hunting grounds of a Beastman warherd. Several woodcutters have vanished, and Fronich, fearing a panic that would shut down his lucrative operation, has been covering up the disappearances and blaming them on 'accidents' or desertion.
hooks: Fronich hires the party as guards for the lumber camp, offering a generous wage. He claims they've had trouble with bandits and wolves, but forbids the party from venturing into the 'deep woods,' insisting the area is too dangerous to patrol.

The wife of a missing woodcutter approaches the party in Ubersreik. Her husband vanished from the Fronich camp two weeks ago, and Fronich claims he ran off with his pay. She doesn't believe it for a second and begs the party to travel to the camp and find out the truth.

locations.name: The Morgentor District
locations.playerDescription: North of the Artisan's Quarter, the grime and noise of industry give way to the clean, orderly streets of the Morgentor District. This respectable quarter, nestled against the walls of the Precinct, is the administrative and financial heart of the town outside of the Town Hall itself. Well-maintained stone buildings house banks, law offices, and the headquarters of the more 'scholarly' guilds. The air is quiet, filled only with the rustle of paper and the murmur of serious business. Watch patrols are a common sight, ensuring the peace is kept for the district's influential inhabitants.
locations.gmNotes: Morgentor, or 'Morning Gate,' is where the real power outside the castles is brokered. Influence here is traded not with swords, but with contracts, loans, and legal writs. The district's proximity to the Precinct means it's heavily influenced by the military, but its lifeblood is the city's commerce. Beneath the veneer of respectability, however, the same struggles for power that plague the rest of Ubersreik play out in backroom deals and shadowy bargains.

locations.name: Brown Beard's Bank
locations.playerDescription: A formidable, windowless granite building that looks more like a small fortress than a bank. A single, iron-banded door is flanked by two impassive Dwarf guards in gleaming mail. The sign, a finely carved slab of slate, reads simply 'Brown Beard's Bank.' It has a reputation for being the most secure place to store valuables in Ubersreik.
locations.gmNotes: The bank is owned and operated by Borin Grudgebearer, a venerable Dwarf longbeard. While scrupulously honest in his business dealings, Borin holds an ancient and bitter grudge against the von Bruner family over a mining rights dispute that cost his clan dearly a century ago. Seeing the current turmoil as an opportunity, Borin is secretly using his vast wealth to fund anti-Altdorf and anti-Jungfreud agitators, hoping to destabilize the city and weaken the von Bruners' standing.
hooks: An agent of Lady Kisaiya von Bruner hires the party for a delicate task: break into Brown Beard's Bank. They don't want to steal gold, but to retrieve an old contract from Borin's personal vault that proves the von Bruners' claim to the disputed mine.

Borin Grudgebearer, seeking deniable agents, hires the party for a simple courier job: deliver a heavy, sealed coffer to a 'patriot' at the Sprichstumpf. The recipient is the firebrand agitator Anton Grimski, and the coffer is full of coin to fund a new wave of riots.

locations.name: The Halls of Justice
locations.playerDescription: A grand, symmetrical building of white stone, its entrance supported by pillars carved with the iconography of Verena and the scales of justice. One wing is designated the Prosecutors' Lodge, the other the Judges' Lodge. Clerks in sober robes hurry up and down the steps, their arms laden with scrolls and books, while lawyers argue cases in hushed but intense tones.
locations.gmNotes: This is the center of Ubersreik's legal system. The Chief Prosecutor, Alaric Haupt, is a brilliant legal mind but a man with a weakness for decadence. He is being blackmailed with evidence of his attendance at a Slaaneshi revel by Andreas von Bruner. The Head Judge, Isolde Richter, is a stern and famously incorruptible woman, but she is old and finds it difficult to navigate the city's new political reality.
hooks: A friend of the party is arrested on trumped-up charges. Their case is assigned to Prosecutor Haupt, who seems intent on securing a guilty verdict regardless of the evidence. The party must discover the source of Haupt's blackmail to have any hope of getting a fair trial.

Judge Richter, unable to trust the compromised Watch or the city's prosecutors, summons the party to her private chambers. She has reason to believe a prominent guild master is a secret chaos cultist and wants the party to conduct a highly illegal and discreet investigation to find proof.

locations.name: Carters' Guild
locations.playerDescription: A large, utilitarian stone building with wide doors to accommodate the comings and goings of carts and wagons. Inside, the air is thick with the smell of hay, leather, and horse sweat. The guildhall serves as a meeting place for carters, a storage facility for goods in transit, and a hub for coordinating deliveries throughout Ubersreik and beyond.
locations.gmNotes: The Carters' Guild is led by Guildmaster Hans Fuhrmann, a close ally of the burgomeister. Fuhrmann is a shrewd and pragmatic man who sees the guild as a vital cog in the city's economy. However, he is also under pressure from both the Altdorf military authorities, who want to control supply lines, and the Lowhaven Clan, who seek to use the guild's resources for smuggling operations. Fuhrmann walks a fine line, trying to keep both sides satisfied while maintaining the guild's independence.
hooks: The party is hired to escort a valuable shipment of supplies from the Carters' Guild to the Altdorf garrison. However, they soon discover that the Lowhaven Clan has plans to intercept the shipment for their own purposes. The party must navigate this dangerous situation and ensure the supplies reach their destination.

Guildmaster Fuhrmann suspects that one of his trusted carters is secretly working for the Lowhaven Clan, smuggling goods under the guild's banner. He hires the party to investigate and gather evidence of the carter's illicit activities, promising a generous reward for their discretion and success.

locations.name: The Old Vixen Tavern
locations.playerDescription: A respectable, quiet tavern known for its expensive wine and discretion. The interior is paneled in dark wood, with numerous curtained booths offering privacy to the clientele of lawyers, city officials, and guild representatives. The air is thick with pipe smoke and the murmur of hushed negotiations.
locations.gmNotes: The owner, 'Mother' Magda, is a sharp-witted woman in her sixties with eyes that miss nothing. The tavern is a major hub for information, and Magda is its foremost broker. She trades in the secrets she overhears, selling them to all sides in the city's struggles. Her primary client is Lady Emmanuelle Nacht, the Imperial Herald, who uses Magda's network to keep a finger on the pulse of the city's political undercurrents.
hooks: The party is hired to disrupt a secret meeting between a representative of the Altdorf army and several guild masters. They must infiltrate the Old Vixen, get past Magda's watchful eyes, and plant a forged document that will sow distrust among the attendees.

The party needs to learn the secret schedule of Watch patrols in the Merchant Quarter. They are told the only person who would know is Mother Magda, but she won't accept coin. She wants them to steal a specific bottle of rare Estalian wine from the cellar of the Bruner Palace.

locations.name: The Gilded Cage
locations.playerDescription: A high-class establishment that glitters with polished brass and red velvet. The ground floor houses a small theatre for plays and musical performances ('Violetta's Variety'), while the upper floors contain an exclusive, high-stakes gambling salon ('Martin's Game House'). The clientele is exclusively the wealthy and powerful, and burly, well-dressed guards ensure no undesirables get past the door.
locations.gmNotes: The Gilded Cage is owned and operated by Martin Violetta, a flamboyant and charming Tilean. However, the entire operation is a front for the Lowhaven Clan. It serves as a way to launder their criminal profits and, more importantly, to ensnare the city's elite in gambling debts, which Mercy Lowhaven then leverages for information and influence. Martin is merely a manager, trapped by his own substantial debts to the Halflings.
hooks: After an incredible run of luck at the card table, a player character wins a massive pot. The house manager, Martin, nervously refuses to pay out, claiming there was a misdeal. Insisting on payment will draw the attention of the Lowhaven's surprisingly brutal Halfling enforcers.

A panicked young noble hires the party. He lost his family's ancestral signet ring in a game of cards to a visiting 'merchant' who was cheating. The 'merchant' was Sunny Lowhaven in disguise, and now Mercy Lowhaven is using the ring to blackmail the noble's family. The party must get the ring back.

locations.name: Neuner's Herbs and Tinctures
locations.playerDescription: A traditional herbalist's shop, with bunches of dried herbs hanging from the rafters and the air filled with a hundred competing earthy aromas. Jars of powders, poultices, and preserved plants line the shelves. Old Man Neuner, a wizened man with dirt under his nails, can be found grinding ingredients with a mortar and pestle.
locations.gmNotes: Neuner is a master herbalist, practicing the craft as his family has for generations. He despises the 'newfangled nonsense' of alchemy and sees his rival, Simon's Pharmacy, as a dangerous perversion of the healing arts. He is a purist and something of a luddite, but his remedies are undeniably effective.
hooks: Neuner has received a rare order from Cordelia's Apothecary for a large quantity of Glimmercap mushrooms, which only grow in a specific, Beastman-infested cave in the Hagercrybs. He is too old to make the journey himself and needs a brave party to harvest them for him.

After a series of his supply shipments are spoiled or go missing, Neuner is convinced his rival Simon is sabotaging him. He wants to hire the party to retaliate by sneaking into Simon's Pharmacy and replacing his stock of refined alchemical reagents with inert, but identical-looking, powders.

locations.name: Simon's Pharmacy
locations.playerDescription: A clean, modern-looking shop with large glass windows displaying neatly arranged bottles of brightly coloured liquids. The air smells of alcohol and strange chemicals. Behind the counter, the young and ambitious Simon von Holtz offers consultations, promising alchemical solutions to any ailment.
locations.gmNotes: Simon is a talented alchemist who was expelled from the Gold Order in Altdorf for conducting unsanctioned experiments. He sees Ubersreik as a provincial backwater, but also an opportunity to make his fortune. He considers traditional herbalists like Neuner to be fools and is not above using underhanded tactics to put his rival out of business and secure the market for himself.
hooks: Simon is trying to create a revolutionary healing draught but lacks a key ingredient: the venom of a Sewer Wyrm, a rare creature said to live in the deepest parts of Ubersreik's sewer network. He offers a substantial reward for a fresh, unspoiled vial of the venom.

One of Simon's 'experimental' potions has had an unforeseen side effect on a wealthy client, who now has shimmering, rainbow-coloured skin. The client has locked himself in his manor and his family hires the party to discreetly bring Simon to the estate to brew an antidote before the scandal becomes public.

locations.name: Stork Loans
locations.playerDescription: A discreet, respectable-looking office with a simple sign depicting a stork carrying a heavy bag of coins. Inside, a well-dressed clerk sits at a polished desk, ready to discuss financial matters with potential clients. The atmosphere is professional and reassuring.
locations.gmNotes: This is a classic honey trap. Herr Stork, a tall, gaunt man who resembles his namesake, runs a ruthless loan shark operation. The business is a subsidiary of The Baron's expanding criminal network, providing her with a foothold in the more respectable parts of town. Stork offers loans at impossible-to-repay rates, then uses a team of brutal enforcers, disguised as 'debt collectors', to seize assets or claim a pound of flesh.
hooks: A contact of the party, perhaps a craftsman or minor merchant, took a loan from Stork to stay afloat and has now defaulted. Thugs have broken his legs and are threatening his family. He begs the party for help before the collectors come back to seize his shop.

Marta Müller, master of the Merchants' Guild, is concerned about Stork's activities and how he is preying on guild members. She hires the party to investigate his operation, find proof of his illegal methods, and, most importantly, discover who he is working for.

locations.name: Ubersreik Builders' Company
locations.playerDescription: A large, busy yard filled with stacks of lumber, blocks of cut stone, and piles of sand and gravel. The air rings with the sound of hammering and sawing. The main office is a simple, functional building where Guildmaster Otto Kessel can be seen arguing with foremen and clients.
locations.gmNotes: The Builders' Company handles all major stone construction in the city. Guildmaster Kessel is a pragmatist who believes a coin is a coin, no matter whose hand it comes from. He has taken lucrative contracts from the Altdorf occupiers to repair the town walls, earning him the scorn of Jungfreud loyalists. He is also in a bitter jurisdictional feud with Ernst Zimmerman's Carpenters' Guild.
hooks: A crane at a major construction site 'accidentally' collapses, killing a foreman. Kessel is convinced it was sabotage by the Carpenters' Guild and hires the party to find proof before the feud escalates into open street brawls between the guilds.

A Jungfreud loyalist group wants to send a message to collaborators. They hire the party to sneak into the Builders' yard at night and burn their supply of seasoned lumber, a costly blow that will delay the Altdorfers' fortification projects.

locations.name: The Enchanter's Wardrobe
locations.playerDescription: An elegant tailor's shop, distinct from any other in Ubersreik. The window displays a single, magnificent robe on a mannequin, its threads seeming to shift and catch the light in impossible ways. Inside, the air is calm and smells of lavender. Bolts of impossibly fine cloth line the walls.
locations.gmNotes: The proprietor is Elara, a High Elf seamstress who came to the Empire centuries ago. She is quiet, graceful, and carries an air of ancient sadness. Elara is a minor practitioner of Elven lore, and she can weave subtle enchantments into her garments — a cloak that billows without wind, a gown that resists stains, gloves that always stay warm. She keeps to herself, but is being watched by agents of Dordean Mournflair's visiting sibling, who is deeply suspicious of any Elf 'meddling' in the Old World.
hooks: Christoph Engel, the Grey Wizard, requires a new set of robes that can help conceal his presence. He needs specific, magically-attuned materials woven into the fabric: the silk of a phase spider and three feathers from a raven that has fed on a wizard's corpse. He hires the party to acquire these rare components for Elara.

A brash young noble bought an enchanted cape from Elara that was meant to enhance his charisma. Instead, he now uncontrollably speaks every thought that enters his head. He storms into the shop with his house guards, accusing Elara of witchcraft and demanding his money back, threatening to escalate the matter to the Witch Hunters.

locations.name: The Blucher Estate
locations.playerDescription: A respectable, walled estate with a finely manicured rose garden and an elegant, if somewhat dated, manor house. The wrought iron gates are emblazoned with a blue shield crest. The estate is quiet, with only a few elderly servants occasionally seen tending the grounds.
locations.gmNotes: This is the ancestral home of Captain Erwin Blucher, the commander of Magnus's Tower. It is currently inhabited by his formidable aunt, Lady Isolde Blucher. Lady Isolde is a staunch supporter of the von Jungfreuds and is utterly ashamed of her nephew's opportunism in siding with the Altdorf invaders. She uses her home to host clandestine 'poetry circles' which are, in fact, strategy meetings for high-ranking Jungfreud loyalists, including Guido Falck.
hooks: Captain Blucher hires the party for a deeply personal and risky mission. Before he left home to join the army, he hid a series of compromising letters from a former lover in a secret compartment in his old bedroom. With his aunt now hosting conspirators, he needs those letters retrieved before they can be found and used against him.

The party is approached by one of Lady Isolde's servants. The next 'poetry circle' is happening tonight, and she has learned that a spy from the Altdorf forces has infiltrated the guest list. The party is hired to attend the gathering, identify the spy, and neutralize them without revealing the true nature of the meeting.

locations.name: The Reuter Estate
locations.playerDescription: A sprawling estate on the outskirts of Ubersreik, surrounded by high stone walls and dense hedges. The main house is a grand, two-story building with large windows and a well-tended garden. The estate exudes an air of old wealth and quiet dignity.
locations.gmNotes: The Reuter Estate is the home of the merchant Albrecht Reuter, a man of considerable wealth and influence. Reuter is a pragmatist who has managed to maintain his business interests through the city's turbulent times by carefully navigating the shifting political landscape. He is known for his discreet dealings with both the Altdorf authorities and the Jungfreud loyalists, making him a valuable ally or a dangerous enemy.
hooks: Rutger Reuter, the son of Albrecht Reuter, has reportedly been killed by the legendary Beast of the Ortschlamm, while he was supervising a windmill construction project outside the city. Albrecht is devastated and hires the party to investigate the circumstances of his son's death, suspecting foul play rather than a mere accident.

Albrecht Reuter hires the party to deliver a sensitive message to a contact within the Altdorf garrison. The message contains information about a planned Jungfreud uprising, and Reuter wants to ensure it reaches the right ears without falling into the wrong hands.

A trusted employee of Reuter's has gone missing, and Reuter fears they may have been kidnapped by Jungfreud loyalists seeking leverage against him. He hires the party to investigate the disappearance and bring his employee back safely.

locations.name: The Araworn's Estate
locations.playerDescription: A grand estate perched on a hill overlooking the city. The main house is an imposing stone structure with tall, narrow windows and a steeply pitched roof. The grounds are meticulously maintained, with manicured lawns, ornate fountains, and a small orchard.
locations.gmNotes: The Araworn Estate is the ancestral home of the Araworn elfs, a family with deep roots in Ubersreik's history. The current head of the family, Thalion Araworn, is a reclusive figure who rarely leaves the estate. He is known for his eccentric interests in ancient lore and arcane studies. The estate itself is rumored to contain hidden chambers and secret libraries filled with forbidden knowledge. In reality, Thalion is a secret member of the Fractured Eye, a cult dedicated to Tzeentch, using his resources to further their inscrutable goals.
hooks: Thalion Araworn has recently acquired a rare and powerful artifact, a crystal orb said to contain visions of the future. However, the orb has attracted unwanted attention from rival factions within the city. Thalion hires the party to act as discreet guards during a private viewing of the orb, ensuring its safety from potential thieves or saboteurs.

A scholar from Altdorf approaches the party with a request. He believes that Thalion Araworn possesses a lost tome of ancient elven magic that could be invaluable to his research. The scholar hires the party to infiltrate the estate and retrieve the tome without alerting Thalion or his staff.

locations.name: The Pious Cup Tearoom
locations.playerDescription: A prim, proper, and spotlessly clean tearoom. The walls are adorned with stern-looking portraits of Magnus the Pious and other famous Sigmarite saints. The clientele consists mainly of devout elderly ladies and the occasional off-duty priest. The air smells of chamomile tea and righteousness. No alcohol is served.
locations.gmNotes: The owner, Greta Schmidt, is a fervent Sigmarite. The tearoom is a front for a cell of the Order of the Cleansing Flame, a secret society of Sigmarite fanatics who believe the established cult is too soft on heresy and corruption. They are the same order as Ernst Ricker, who lurks in the High Temple's basement. They use the tearoom to identify new recruits and plan their own unsanctioned purges against those they deem heretical.
hooks: The party overhears a group of patrons in the tearoom discussing the 'moral failings' of a local artisan and the need for 'Sigmar's fire to cleanse the wicked.' The next day, the artisan's workshop is burned to the ground. The Watch rules it an accident, but the artisan's family suspects otherwise and hires the party to investigate.

Father Emming is concerned about the pious young priestess, Irma Brantl. She has started attending 'special prayer meetings' at the Pious Cup. Fearing she is falling in with extremists, he asks the party to discreetly attend the next meeting and report back on what is really being discussed.

locations.name: The Stiegler House
locations.playerDescription: A modest, well-kept townhouse just between the Artisans' Quarter and the Morgentor District. The exterior is plain, with little decoration aside from a small brass plaque beside the door bearing the family name 'Stiegler.' Inside, the house is in a constant state of panic, with papers strewn about and a general air of disarray.
locations.gmNotes: The Stiegler House is the home of the Stiegler family, an up and coming merchant family from Grausee, a village not far-distant from Ubersreik. The patriarch, Wilhelm Stiegler, recently moved his family to the city to expand his trading business. However, Wilhelm has become increasingly paranoid, convinced that rival merchants and guilds are plotting against him. In reality, Wilhelm has fallen under the influence of a minor chaos cult that preys on his fears, urging him to take drastic measures to 'protect' his family and business. Johanna, his daughter, is unaware of her father's descent into madness and struggles to keep the family together amidst the turmoil. She recently departed for a new windmill project with Rutger Reuter, hoping to find some peace and stability away from her father's increasingly erratic behaviour.
hooks: Wilhelm Stiegler has disappeared, leaving behind a frantic note warning of an imminent threat to his family. Johanna hires the party to find her father and bring him back safely, fearing that his paranoia has led him into danger.

The party is approached by a mysterious figure who claims to have information about Wilhelm Stiegler's involvement with a chaos cult. They offer to share this information in exchange for a favour: retrieve a specific item from the Stiegler House without alerting the family.

locations.name: Guild of Horologists and Cogsmiths
locations.playerDescription: A narrow, tall building with a massive, ornate clock face built into its facade, which somehow manages to show the correct time. From within, a constant, gentle cacophony of a thousand ticking, whirring, and chiming mechanisms can be heard. The ground floor is a shop displaying marvels of clockwork, from tiny automated songbirds to grand father clocks.
locations.gmNotes: Guildmaster Thadeus Mitzeltot is a man obsessed with precision, order, and time. This obsession has led him to become a secret devotee of a minor cult of Astasis, an obscure deity of absolute stasis and law. Thadeus believes chaos is the ultimate evil and that every action should be pre-ordained and measured. He uses his skills to build incredibly complex clockwork listening devices, which he hides inside the clocks he sells to Ubersreik's most powerful citizens, gathering information for his own inscrutable purposes.
hooks: The Burgomeister, Ernst Maler, suspects someone is leaking information from his private office in the Town Hall. The only recent addition to the room is a magnificent new clock, a gift from the guild. He hires the party to investigate the clock and its maker without causing a public scandal.

Thadeus is building his masterpiece: a clock that can, he believes, calculate the future. It requires a 'Heart of Crystal,' a perfectly regular crystal formation found only in a Skaven-infested abandoned mine. He will pay an astronomical sum for this component, claiming it is for a commission for a Nuln baron.

locations.name: Relics & Reveries
locations.playerDescription: A cramped, dusty antique shop overflowing with a bizarre collection of items: a stuffed two-headed calf, a tarnished suit of Tilean armour, stacks of yellowed books, and countless other curiosities. The air is thick with the smell of decay and forgotten things. The shopkeeper, Caspian, is a man of indeterminate age with mismatched eyes who seems to appear from the shadows whenever a customer touches something.
locations.gmNotes: Caspian is an unaligned servant of Tzeentch, the Changer of Ways. He is not part of any organized cult but a 'Dilettante' who delights in sowing subtle chaos. He trades in items with strange histories and minor curses, finding joy in seeing how these objects change the lives of their new owners. The shop itself is a minor nexus of chaotic energy, and its layout seems to shift when no one is looking.
hooks: While browsing, a party member finds an item they lost years ago in a completely different part of the Empire. Caspian smiles and says, 'It found its way here.' He will not sell it for money, but will trade it for 'an object of equal emotional significance' from the character's current possessions.

The party is hired by Ludwig Schlüsselfert, the locksmith. He has been tasked with opening a puzzle box that has defied all his attempts. He traced its origin to Caspian's shop. Caspian claims he cannot remember the box, but will gladly sell them a 'key that opens not what is locked, but what is hidden' for a steep price.

locations.name: The Seven Veils
locations.playerDescription: An esoteric bookshop, its windows painted over with complex astrological charts and arcane symbols. A faint, sweet smell of incense wafts from beneath the door. The sign above depicts a seven-pointed star. Inside, the shop is dimly lit, filled with strange books, star-charts, and occult paraphernalia.
locations.gmNotes: The shop is run by Friedrich von Happe, a well-spoken scholar and astrologer. It is a recruitment front for the Order of the Unblinking Eye, the Slaaneshi cult that counts Andreas von Bruner among its members. Friedrich uses his position to identify citizens with hidden lusts and ambitions, offering them 'forbidden knowledge' and 'paths to true fulfillment' that lead them straight into the cult's perfumed embrace.
hooks: A young scribe from the Town Hall has gone missing. His worried family last saw him heading to The Seven Veils for an 'astrological reading.' They hire the party to find out what has happened to him.

The party is given a package to deliver to the shop by a hooded figure, who pays them well and asks no questions. The package writhes slightly and emits a faint moan. Inside the shop, Friedrich is expecting them and offers them a glass of exquisite, strangely intoxicating wine while he inspects the delivery.

locations.name: The Artisan's Repose
locations.playerDescription: A large, well-organized store that serves as a high-end supplier for the city's master craftsmen. There are no common goods here; instead, one can find rare hardwoods from the Laurelorn Forest, billets of gromril-veined iron, and tools of unparalleled quality. Access is restricted to guild members, and the prices are astronomical.
locations.gmNotes: The store is managed by a consortium of the city's main craft guilds, but this cooperation is a thin veneer over a hotbed of intense rivalry. The store's fussy manager, Klaus, is an expert at playing the guilds against each other. For a small bribe, he will provide information on what materials a rival guild is purchasing, offering clues to their secret projects and commissions. He is currently on the payrolls of at least three different guild masters.
hooks: Rudy Schlau, master of the Cutlers' Guild, hires the party for an act of industrial espionage. He wants them to get into The Artisan's Repose and find the purchase ledger to see what kind of steel Petronilla Merkle and the Metalworkers' Guild have been buying, suspecting they have found a new source.

A shipment of rare wood has been stolen en route to the store. The guilds are blaming each other, and tensions are high. Klaus, fearing the loss of business, pools a reward from the guilds and hires the party to track down the real thieves and recover the cargo before the situation devolves into open conflict.

locations.name: The Ubersreik Patriot's Club
locations.playerDescription: An unassuming but well-kept townhouse with a small, discreet brass plaque reading 'Ubersreik Patriot's Club.' Inside, the rooms are decorated with faded von Jungfreud banners, portraits of the Duke, and maps of the Duchy. A few grim-faced men and women sit in quiet conversation, sipping ale and looking suspiciously at any newcomers.
locations.gmNotes: This is one of Guido Falck's Jungfreud resistance movement's secret headquarters. While posing as a social club for those with 'traditionalist sympathies,' it is one of the nerve center for planning acts of sabotage against the Altdorf occupiers, printing seditious pamphlets, and coordinating with loyalists throughout the city. The members are dedicated but paranoid, and desperately short on weapons and coin.
hooks: If the party has gained a reputation for being anti-Altdorf, they are approached by a club member and invited to a meeting. Guido Falck will offer them a dangerous mission: raid a warehouse owned by the Duane Brothers to steal a shipment of black powder meant for the Altdorf garrison.

Captain Andrea Pfeffer of the Watch has her suspicions about the club but lacks the political clout to raid it openly. She hires the party as deniable agents to infiltrate the club, pose as sympathizers, and gather concrete proof of their seditious activities, or better yet, the location of Guido Falck himself.

locations.name: Duane Brothers Shipping & Haulage
locations.playerDescription: A large, muddy yard dominated by a sprawling warehouse and stables. Wagons are in constant motion, being loaded and unloaded by a small army of sweating labourers. Bellowing orders over the chaos are the two Duane brothers, Otto and Ulli, a pair of massive, identical men with furious tempers and fists the size of hams.
locations.gmNotes: The Duane Brothers have secured the highly lucrative contract to handle all logistics for the occupying Altdorf army. They are growing rich, but their collaboration has made them pariahs among many locals. They are also fantastically corrupt, routinely skimming from army shipments and selling the stolen goods on the black market through intermediaries connected to the Lowhaven Clan.
hooks: A quartermaster in the Altdorf army is convinced he's being shorted on supplies but can't prove it. He hires the party to get jobs as labourers in the Duane Brothers' yard, hoping they can find evidence of the theft from the inside.

The brothers are trying to buy out a smaller, rival haulage company. When the owner refuses, his prize-winning draft horse has its legs broken. The owner hires the party for protection, fearing the Duane Brothers' next move will be against him and his family.

locations.name: The Magnusson Collegiate School
locations.playerDescription: A large, three-story building of grey stone, its seriousness broken by the sounds of children shouting and playing in the walled yard. This is the premier school for the children of Ubersreik's prosperous citizens: merchants, guild leaders, and bureaucrats. Through the windows, you can see classrooms where stern-faced tutors drill students in letters and numbers.
locations.gmNotes: The school is run by Headmaster Albus Posen, a gentle scholar and devout follower of Verena, the goddess of wisdom. He genuinely believes that education and rational discourse can solve any problem. However, the school has become a bitter microcosm of the city's political division. The children of Jungfreud loyalists have formed gangs that fight the children of 'collaborators.' Posen is struggling to maintain order as playground squabbles escalate into politically-charged violence.
hooks: After a particularly nasty brawl in the schoolyard where a child's arm was broken, Headmaster Posen hires the party to act as 'groundskeepers.' Their real job is to provide security, mediate disputes, and try to uncover which parents are encouraging their children's violent behavior.

A priceless, illuminated history of the von Jungfreud line has been stolen from the school's locked library. Posen is terrified of the political fallout if the theft becomes public. He suspects one of the older, more radicalized students and needs the party to investigate the theft quietly and recover the book before it is destroyed or used for seditious purposes.
